h001.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: 'Shall I not teach you the most superior surah in the Quran before you leave the mosque?' He took my hand, and when we were about to leave I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you said you would teach me the most superior surah in the Quran.' He said: 'Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil Alamin — The Seven Oft-Repeated Verses and the Magnificent Quran that has been given to me.'
h001.book: Book of Virtues of the Quran
h001.topic: Al-Fatiha is the greatest surah in the Quran

h002.text: Allah the Exalted said: 'I have divided the prayer between Myself and My servant in two halves, and My servant shall have what he asks for.' When the servant says 'All praise is due to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds,' Allah says: My servant has praised Me. When he says 'The Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful,' Allah says: My servant has extolled Me. When he says 'Master of the Day of Recompense,' Allah says: My servant has glorified Me. When he says 'You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help,' Allah says: This is between Me and My servant, and My servant shall have what he asks for. When he says 'Guide us to the straight path, the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour, not of those who have evoked Your anger or of those who are astray,' Allah says: This is for My servant, and My servant shall have what he has asked for.
h002.topic: Allah's direct response to each verse of Al-Fatiha during prayer

h003.text: Some Companions stopped near an Arab tribe. The chief of the tribe was bitten by a snake or scorpion. A man from among them went to the Companions and said: 'Do any of you know medicine or a ruqyah?' They agreed to treat him in exchange for a flock of sheep. One of them began reciting Surah Al-Fatiha, gathering his saliva and spitting on the bite site. The man recovered immediately. When they told the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: 'How did you know that it could be used as a ruqyah? Divide the sheep among yourselves, and give me a share as well.' And he smiled.
h003.topic: Al-Fatiha as a healing and ruqyah (spiritual remedy)

h004.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever does not recite Al-Fatiha in his prayer, his prayer is invalid.'
h004.book: Book of the Characteristics of Prayer
h004.topic: Al-Fatiha is obligatory in every unit of prayer

h005.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When the Imam says Ameen, say Ameen, for whoever's Ameen coincides with that of the angels, all his previous sins will be forgiven.'
h005.book: Book of the Call to Prayer
h005.topic: Saying Ameen at the end of Al-Fatiha

h010.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked: 'O Abu Mundhir! Do you know which verse of the Book of Allah that you have memorised is greatest?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He asked again: 'O Abu Mundhir! Which verse of the Book of Allah that you have memorised is greatest?' I said: 'Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence [Ayat al-Kursi].' He struck me on the chest and said: 'By Allah, may knowledge be pleasant for you, O Abu Mundhir!'
h010.book: Book of the Prayer of Travellers
h010.topic: Ayat al-Kursi is the greatest verse in the Quran

h011.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) assigned me to guard the zakah of Ramadan. A figure came and began taking food stealthily. I seized him and said I would take him to the Prophet. He pleaded poverty and need. This happened three times. On the third occasion he said: 'Let me go and I will teach you words by which Allah will benefit you. When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi in full. A guardian from Allah will then be over you all night, and no devil will come near you until morning.' When I told the Prophet, he said: 'He told you the truth, even though he is a liar. Do you know who you were speaking with for three nights, O Abu Hurairah? That was the devil.'
h011.book: Book of the Virtues of the Quran
h011.topic: Ayat al-Kursi protects from the devil through the night

h012.text: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi at the end of every obligatory prayer, nothing will stand between him and entering Paradise except death.'
h012.book: Book of the Day and Night
h012.topic: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer

h020.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Gather together, for I am going to recite to you one third of the Quran.' Those who could came and gathered. He came out, recited 'Say: He is Allah, the One,' then went back in. Some said to one another: 'Perhaps a revelation came to him from the sky.' He then came out again and said: 'I told you I would recite one third of the Quran to you. Verily, this surah is equal to one third of the Quran.'
h020.book: Book of the Prayer of Travellers
h020.topic: Surah Al-Ikhlas equals one third of the Quran in reward

isnad.name: Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman (d. 94 AH)

h021.text: A man from the Ansar used to lead his community in prayer at the Quba mosque. Whenever he recited an opening surah for a rak'ah, he would follow it by reciting 'Say: He is Allah, the One' before reciting any other surah, doing this in every rak'ah. The people complained to the Prophet (ﷺ), who summoned the man and asked why he did this. The man replied: 'I love this surah.' The Prophet said: 'Your love for it will admit you to Paradise.'
h021.topic: Loving Surah Al-Ikhlas is a path to Paradise

h022.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent a man on an expedition as commander of a group. He used to lead his companions in prayer and would always end his recitation with 'Say: He is Allah, the One.' When they returned and mentioned this to the Prophet, he said: 'Ask him why he did that.' They asked him, and he replied: 'Because it is the attribute of the Merciful, and I love to recite it.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Tell him that Allah loves him.'
h022.topic: Allah loves those who love Surah Al-Ikhlas

h030.text: On the night of al-Aqabah, the Prophet (ﷺ) revealed to me: 'Has the surah of al-Baqarah not come to you with the two verses at the end of it? These were not given to any prophet before me.' Then he said: 'Allah — there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence...' down to 'And He is the Most High, the Most Great.'
h030.topic: The special status of Ayat al-Kursi, given to no prophet before

h031.text: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Abu Dharr, shall I tell you the best thing by which you can protect yourself each evening? It is Ayat al-Kursi — whoever reads it will be under Allah's protection until morning, and whoever reads it in the morning will be under Allah's protection until evening.'
h031.topic: Ayat al-Kursi at morning and evening for daily protection

h040.text: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to raise his head from the last prostration in Fajr prayer, he would recite: 'O Allah, indeed I ask You for the mercy from Your presence by which You guide my heart, unite my affairs, gather what is scattered of me, return what is absent, raise what is lowered, strengthen what is weak, make what is near firm, purify what is corrupt, and inspire in me my right guidance...' He continued with a long supplication that included seeking refuge in Allah from every evil companion and partner in worldly affairs and the Hereafter.

h100.text: Whoever recites Ya-Sin in the night will wake up forgiven, and whoever recites Ha Mim, in which Ad-Dukhan (the Smoke) is mentioned, will wake up forgiven.
h100.topic: Virtue of reciting Surah Ya-Sin at night

h101.text: When the son of Adam dies, all his deeds come to an end except three: knowledge which is beneficial to others, a righteous child who prays for him, or ongoing charity which he leaves behind.
h101.topic: Deeds that continue after death as one's traces

h102.text: O Banu Salamah, stay where you are, and your footsteps will be recorded; stay where you are, and your footsteps will be recorded.
h102.topic: Footsteps to the mosque are recorded as traces

h103.text: The Prophet asked, 'O Abu Dharr! Do you know where the sun sets?' I said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, and that is the meaning of Allah's saying: And the sun runs on its fixed course for a term. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.'
h103.topic: The sun's fixed course beneath the Throne

h104.text: The Prophet smiled and said, 'Do you know why I am smiling? Because of the way a servant will argue with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He will say, "O Lord, will You not protect me from injustice?" Allah will say, "Of course." He will say, "I will not accept any witness against me except from myself." Allah will say, "Today you will be a sufficient witness against yourself, and the honorable scribes will serve as witnesses against you." Then his mouth will be sealed, and it will be said to his limbs, "Speak!" So they will speak of what he did. Then he will be permitted to speak and will say, "May you be doomed! It was for you that I was fighting."'
h104.topic: Mouths sealed and limbs bearing witness on Judgement Day

h105.text: When death approached a man and he lost all hope of life, he instructed his family: 'When I die, gather a lot of firewood and set it ablaze until my flesh is consumed and my bones become brittle. Then take them, grind them, and scatter them in the sea.' So they did that, but Allah gathered him together and said to him, 'Why did you do that?' He said, 'Out of fear of You.' So Allah forgave him.
h105.topic: Allah's power to resurrect scattered remains

h106.text: Verily, there is a chapter in the Qur'an which contains thirty Ayat that will intercede on behalf of its reciter until he is forgiven. It is: 'Blessed be He in Whose Hand is the dominion.'
h106.topic: Surah Al-Mulk intercedes for its reciter

h107.text: There is a chapter of the Qur'an that will argue on behalf of its reciter until it causes him to enter Paradise. It is: 'Blessed be He in Whose Hand is the dominion.'
h107.topic: Surah Al-Mulk argues for its reciter until Paradise

h108.text: There are seven people whom Allah will shade in the shade of His Throne on the Day when there will be no shade except its shade. Among them are: a man who is tempted by a beautiful woman of high social status but says, 'Verily, I fear Allah,' and a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spent.
h108.topic: The seven whom Allah will shade on the Day of Judgement

h109.text: If you would trust in Allah as He truly should be trusted in, He would surely provide for you as He provides for the birds. They set out in the morning with empty stomachs and return in the evening with full stomachs.
h109.topic: True reliance upon Allah (tawakkul) brings provision

h110.text: It was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, how will the people be gathered on their faces?' He replied, 'Is not He who made them walk on their legs able to make them walk on their faces?'
h110.topic: Allah's power to gather the disbelievers upon their faces

h111.text: Al-Qaswa' has not become stubborn, for that is not part of her character. Rather, she has been stopped by He Who restrained the Elephant (of Abrahah).

h112.text: Verily, Allah restrained the Elephant from Makkah, and He has given His Messenger and the believers authority over it. And indeed its sacredness has returned just as it was sacred yesterday. So, let those who are present inform those who are absent.

h113.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) went out to the valley of Al-Batha and ascended the mountain, then cried out, 'O people, come at once!' So the Quraysh gathered around him. He said, 'If I told you all that the enemy was going to attack you in the morning, or in the evening, would you all believe me?' They replied, 'Yes.' Then he said, 'Verily, I am a warner sent to you all before the coming of a severe torment.' Then Abu Lahab said, 'Have you gathered us for this? May you perish!' So Allah revealed: 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab and perish he!' to the end of the Surah.
h113.topic: The warning on the mountain and the cause of revelation

h114.text: Rabi'ah bin 'Abbad said: I saw the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the time of pre-Islamic ignorance in the market of Dhul-Majaz, and he was saying, 'O people! Say there is no god worthy of worship except Allah and you will be successful.' The people were gathered around him, and behind him was a man with a bright face who was saying, 'Verily, he is an apostate and a liar!' This man was following him wherever he went, and he was his uncle, Abu Lahab.
h114.topic: The Prophet's call to Tawhid and Abu Lahab's opposition

h115.text: Asma' bint Abi Bakr said: When 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab' was revealed, the one-eyed Umm Jamil bint Harb came out wailing with a stone in her hand. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was sitting in the Masjid with Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said, 'O Messenger of Allah! She is coming and I fear she will see you.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) replied, 'Verily, she will not see me.' Then he recited some of the Qur'an as a protection for himself. So she stood in front of Abu Bakr and did not see the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him).
h115.topic: Allah's protection of the Prophet from Umm Jamil

h116.text: That which is between the two blowings is forty. Then Allah will send down a rain from the sky and the dead bodies will sprout just as a green plant sprouts. Every part of man will deteriorate except for one bone, and it is the coccyx (tailbone). From it the creation will be assembled on the Day of Judgement.
h116.topic: The two blowings of the Trumpet and the resurrection from the coccyx

h117.text: And none will speak on that Day except the Messengers.
h117.topic: Only the Messengers will speak on the Day of Judgement

h119.text: He who recites the Qur'an proficiently will be with the noble, righteous, ambassador angels, and the one who recites it with difficulty will receive two rewards.
h119.source: Recorded by Imam Ahmad; reported by the group
h119.topic: Reward for reciting the Qur'an and being with the noble angels

isnad.name: Recorded by Imam Ahmad; reported by the group

h120.text: All of the Sons of Adam will decay except for the bone of the coccyx (tailbone). From it he was created and by it he will be reconstructed.
h120.topic: The body decays except the tailbone, from which man is resurrected

h121.text: You will all be gathered barefoot, naked, walking and uncircumcised. When asked whether people would look at one another's nakedness, he replied: Every man among them on that Day will have enough worries to make him careless of others.
h121.topic: People gathered naked on the Day of Resurrection, too preoccupied to notice others

h122.text: Whoever wishes to look at the Day of Judgement as if he is seeing it with his own eyes, then let him read: When the sun is wound round (81:1), and When the heaven is cleft asunder (82:1), and When the heaven is split asunder (84:1).
h122.topic: Reciting Surat At-Takwir and the Day of Judgement

h123.text: The sun and the moon will be rolled up on the Day of Judgement.
h123.topic: The rolling up of the sun and moon

h124.text: "And when the souls are joined with their mates" means those who are alike: every man will be with every group of people who performed the same deeds that he did, because Allah says, "And you (all) will be in three groups" (56:7), they are those who are alike.
h124.topic: Joining of the souls with their mates

h125.text: The Prophet said he was about to prohibit sexual relations with breastfeeding women, but he saw that the Romans and the Persians did so and it did not harm their children at all. When asked about coitus interruptus, he said: That is the minor infanticide, and it is the female infant buried alive (Al-Maw'udah) that will be questioned.
h125.topic: The buried female infant who is questioned

h126.text: Qays bin 'Asim came to the Messenger of Allah and said, O Messenger of Allah, I buried some daughters of mine alive in the period of pre-Islamic ignorance. The Prophet said: Free a slave for each one of them. Qays said, O Messenger of Allah, I am an owner of camels. The Prophet said: Then sacrifice a camel for each one of them.
h126.topic: Atonement for burying infant girls alive

h127.text: I prayed the Morning prayer behind the Prophet, and I heard him reciting: But nay! I swear by Al-Khunnas, Al-Jawar Al-Kunnas, and by the night when it 'As'as, and by the day when it Tanaffas (81:15-18).
h127.topic: The Prophet's recitation of Surat At-Takwir in prayer

h128.text: Mu'adh stood and led the people in the night prayer, and he made his recitation long. So the Prophet said: 'Are you putting the people to trial, O Mu'adh? Why don't you recite (Glorify the Name of your Lord the Most High), (By the forenoon), and (When the heaven is cleft asunder)?'

h131.text: The Messenger of Allah spat in his palm, placed his finger on it, and said: Allah the Mighty and Sublime says: 'O Son of Adam! How can you escape Me when I created you from something similar to this? Then I fashioned you and made your creation balanced so that you walked between two garments, and the earth has a burial place for you. So you gathered wealth and withheld it until your soul reached your collarbone, then at that time you say, I will give charity now. But how will there be time for charity?'
h131.topic: Allah's perfect creation of man and delayed charity

h132.text: A man said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my wife has given birth to a black boy.' The Prophet said: 'Do you have any camels?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'What color are they?' He said: 'Red.' He said: 'Do any of them have patches of gray?' He said: 'Yes.' He asked: 'How did this happen to them?' The man replied: 'It is probably an inherited strain.' The Prophet said: 'Likewise, this is probably an inherited strain.'
h132.topic: The form in which Allah composes a person

h134.text: This will be the Day that mankind will stand before the Lord of all that exists, until one of them will sink up to the middle of his ears in sweat.
h134.topic: Mankind standing before the Lord of all that exists on the Day of Judgement

h135.text: On the Day of Judgement, the sun will draw near the servants until it is a mile or two away from them. Then the sun will burn them, and they will be submersed in sweat based upon the amount of their deeds. Among them there will be those whose sweat will come up to their two heels, those whose sweat will come up to their two knees, those whose sweat will come up to their groins, and those who will be bridled in sweat up to their necks.
h135.topic: The nearness of the sun and people drowning in sweat on the Day of Judgement

h137.text: Woe unto whoever speaks and lies in order to make the people laugh. Woe unto him, woe unto him.
h137.topic: Warning against lying to make people laugh

h138.text: Verily, when the servant commits a sin, a black spot appears in his heart. If he repents from it, his heart is polished clean. But if he increases in the sin, the spot will continue to increase until it overcomes his heart. That is the Ran (covering) that Allah mentions in His statement.
h138.source: At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir
h138.topic: Sins as a black covering (Ran) over the heart

isnad.name: At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Jarir

h139.text: The Messenger of Allah used to begin his late night prayer by declaring Allah's greatness ten times, praising Allah ten times, glorifying Allah ten times, and seeking Allah's forgiveness ten times, then he would say: 'O Allah! Forgive me, guide me, provide for me, and protect me.' Then he would seek refuge from the hardship of the standing on the Day of Judgement.
h139.source: Sunan Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah
h139.topic: Seeking refuge from the hardship of standing on the Day of Judgement

isnad.name: Sunan Abu Dawud, An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah

h140.text: Abu Hurayrah, while leading the people in prayer, recited "When the heaven is split asunder" and prostrated during its recitation. After the prayer he informed them that the Messenger of Allah used to prostrate during its recitation.
h140.topic: Prostration of recitation in Surat Al-Inshiqaq

h141.text: Abu Rafi' reported that he prayed the Night prayer with Abu Hurayrah, who recited "When the heaven is split asunder" and then prostrated. When Abu Rafi' questioned him about it, Abu Hurayrah replied, "I prostrated behind Abul-Qasim (the Prophet), and I will never cease prostrating during its recitation until I meet him."
h141.topic: Prostration of recitation in Surat Al-Inshiqaq

h142.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Jibril said, "O Muhammad! Live how you wish, for verily you will die; love what you wish, for verily you will part with it; and do what you wish, for verily you will meet it (your deed)."
h142.topic: Man returning to his Lord and meeting his deeds

h143.text: The Messenger of Allah said, "Whoever is interrogated during the reckoning will be punished." A'ishah asked, "But did not Allah say, 'He surely will receive an easy reckoning'?" The Prophet replied, "That is not the Reckoning; rather it is the presentation. Whoever is interrogated during the Reckoning on the Day of Judgement will be punished."
h143.topic: The easy reckoning is the presentation, not interrogation

h144.text: The Messenger of Allah said: The time of Al-Maghrib (prayer) lasts as long as Ash-Shafaq (the redness of the horizon) has not disappeared.

h145.text: Ibn 'Abbas explained "You shall certainly travel from stage to stage" as meaning stage after stage, and said: Your Prophet has said this.

h146.text: The Messenger of Allah said: "(And by the Promised Day) refers to the Day of Judgement; (And by the Witness) refers to Friday, and the sun does not rise or set on a day better than Friday, during which there is an hour when no Muslim servant asks Allah for some good but that He gives it to him, and he seeks no refuge from evil but that He protects him; and (And by the Witnessed) refers to the Day of 'Arafah."
h146.topic: Meaning of the Promised Day, the Witness, and the Witnessed

h147.text: The Messenger of Allah narrated the story of a people before us: a king had a sorcerer who, when old, asked for a boy to teach magic. On his way the boy would sit with a monk and admired his words. The boy killed a beast blocking the people's path with a stone after praying that Allah let the monk's way prevail, and the monk told him he would be tested and must not betray him. The boy healed the blind and the lepers, saying only Allah cures, and called people to believe in Allah. When the king learned of this he tortured the courtier, the monk, and the boy; he sawed the monk and the blind man in two. The boy was saved when a mountain shook and when a boat's crew drowned. The boy told the king he could only be killed by gathering the people and shooting an arrow saying, 'In the Name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.' The king did so, the boy died, and the people proclaimed faith in the Lord of the boy. The king then had ditches dug and fires kindled, throwing in all who would not recant, and an infant spoke to its mother: 'Be patient, mother, for you are following the truth!'
h147.topic: The story of the boy, the sorcerer, the monk, and the People of the Ditch

h148.text: Mu'adh led the Maghrib prayer and recited Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa'. So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "Are you putting the people to trial, O Mu'adh? Was it not sufficient for you to recite 'By the heaven and At-Tariq' (At-Tariq), and 'By the sun and its brightness' (Ash-Shams), and the like of them?"
h148.topic: Recitation of moderate-length surahs in prayer; the virtue of Surat At-Tariq

h149.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Every betrayer will have a flag raised for him behind his back, and it will be said, 'This is the betrayal of so-and-so, the son of so-and-so.'"
h149.topic: The Day when secrets are examined; the exposure of treachery on the Day of Judgement

h150.text: The Messenger of Allah said to Mu'adh: "Why didn't you recite 'Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High,' and 'By the sun and its brightness,' and 'By the night when it envelopes.'"
h150.topic: Reciting Al-A'la and similar short surahs in prayer

h151.text: The Messenger of Allah used to recite Surat Al-A'la (chapter 87) and Surat Al-Ghashiyah (chapter 88) in the two 'Id prayers. If the 'Id prayer fell on Friday, he would recite them in both prayers, the 'Id prayer and the Jumu'ah prayer.
h151.source: Muslim, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah
h151.topic: Reciting Al-A'la in the two Eid prayers and Jumu'ah

isnad.name: Muslim, Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, An-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah

h152.narrator: Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza, and 'A'ishah
h152.text: The Messenger of Allah used to recite in the Witr prayer 'Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High,' and 'Say: O you who disbelieve,' and 'Say: He is Allah, the One.' In 'A'ishah's version she added that he would also recite the Mu'awwidhatayn (Al-Falaq and An-Nas).
h152.topic: Surahs the Prophet recited in the Witr prayer

isnad.name: Ubayy bin Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, 'Abdur-Rahman bin Abza, and 'A'ishah

h153.text: Verily, Allah ordained the measure of all creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was over the water.
h153.topic: Allah's decree and measuring of creation

h154.text: Concerning the people of the Fire who are deserving of it, they will neither die nor live. But as for people whom Allah wishes mercy, He will cause them to die in the Fire; then the intercessors will be permitted, and they will be brought group after group and scattered over the rivers of Paradise. It will be said, 'O people of Paradise, pour down upon them,' and they will sprout like the growing of a seed on the moist bank of a flowing stream.
h154.topic: The people of the Fire and the intercession

h155.text: Whoever loves his worldly life will suffer in his Hereafter, and whoever loves his Hereafter will suffer in his worldly life. Therefore, choose that which is everlasting over that which is temporal.
h155.topic: Preferring the Hereafter over the worldly life

h156.text: Do not turn your houses into graves. Verily, Shaytan does not enter the house in which Surat Al-Baqarah is recited.

h157.text: Whoever recites the last two verses of Surat Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him.
h157.topic: Virtue of the last two verses of Al-Baqarah

h158.text: On the night journey, the Messenger of Allah was given three things: the five daily prayers, the closing verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness for those of his Ummah who do not associate any partner with Allah.
h158.topic: The closing verses of Al-Baqarah given at the Isra

h159.text: Islam is built upon five pillars: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the Zakah, fasting Ramadan, and performing Hajj to the House.

h160.text: Take the pre-dawn meal, for there is a blessing in the Suhur.
h160.topic: Encouragement to eat the pre-dawn meal

h161.text: Adi bin Hatim asked about the white thread and the black thread mentioned in the verse, and whether they were actual threads. The Prophet explained that they are not literal threads but rather the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day.
h161.topic: Meaning of the white and black thread of dawn

h162.text: Ibn Mas'ud asked the Prophet which deed is most beloved to Allah. He said, 'The prayer at its proper time.' He asked what is next, and he said, 'Dutifulness to one's parents.' He asked what is next, and he said, 'Jihad in the cause of Allah.'
h162.topic: Praying on time is the most beloved deed

h163.text: Any woman who asks her husband for divorce without a valid reason, the fragrance of Paradise will be forbidden to her.
h163.topic: Warning against seeking divorce without cause

h164.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited this verse, then said: When you see those who follow what is not entirely clear of the Qur'an, then they are those whom Allah described, so beware of them.
h164.topic: Those who follow the unclear verses

h165.text: The best woman of her time was Maryam, the daughter of 'Imran, and the best woman of her time is Khadijah, the daughter of Khuwaylid.

h166.text: When the people of Najran declined the mutual invocation and asked for a trustworthy man, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: I will surely send with you a man who is truly trustworthy. The Companions all hoped to be chosen. He said: Stand up, O Abu 'Ubaydah bin Al-Jarrah. When he stood, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: This is the trustee of this Ummah.

h167.text: When Abu Talhah offered his most beloved property, the Bayruha' garden, in charity, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Well done! That is profitable property, that is profitable property. I have heard what you said, and I think you should give it to your kith and kin. So Abu Talhah distributed it among his relatives.

h168.text: Allah said: I am as My servant thinks of Me.

h169.text: Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; and if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

h170.text: Allah never sent any Prophet nor appointed any successor (Khalifah) but he had two types of confidants: a confidant who enjoined good upon him and urged him to it, and a confidant who enjoined evil upon him and urged him to it. The one protected is he whom Allah protects.

h171.text: The strong person is not the one who overcomes people by his strength; rather, the strong person is the one who controls himself when he is angry.

h172.text: The souls of the martyrs are inside green birds that have lamps suspended beneath the Throne, and they roam freely in Paradise wherever they wish, then return to those lamps. Their Lord looked upon them and asked: Do you wish for anything? They said: What more could we wish for, while we roam freely in Paradise wherever we wish? He asked them this three times, and when they saw that they would not be left without answering, they said: O Lord, we wish that our souls be returned to our bodies so that we may be killed in Your cause once more. When He saw that they had no further need, they were left.
h172.topic: The martyrs are alive with their Lord

h173.text: Whoever Allah gives wealth but he does not pay its Zakah, on the Day of Resurrection his wealth will be made into a bald poisonous male snake with two black spots over its eyes; it will encircle his neck and seize his jaws, saying: I am your wealth, I am your treasure. Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) recited this verse.

h174.text: Ghilan bin Salamah ath-Thaqafi had ten wives when he embraced Islam, and the Prophet said to him: Choose any four of them and divorce the rest.

h175.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Avoid the seven destructive sins. They asked: What are they, O Messenger of Allah? He said: Associating others with Allah, magic, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except in justice, consuming interest, consuming an orphan's wealth, fleeing from the battlefield at the time of fighting, and slandering chaste believing women.

h176.text: When Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas, who was gravely ill and had only one daughter, asked whether he could give two-thirds of his wealth in charity, the Prophet said no; then half, he said no; then one-third, and he said: One-third, and even one-third is too much. It is better to leave your heirs wealthy than to leave them poor, begging from others.

h177.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Suckling makes unlawful what birth makes unlawful.

h178.text: The Messenger of Allah prohibited the temporary (Mut'ah) marriage and the eating of the meat of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar.

h179.text: The Messenger of Allah said to me: Recite the Qur'an to me. I said: Shall I recite it to you when it was revealed to you? He said: I like to hear it from others. So I recited Surat an-Nisa until I reached the verse, How will it be when We bring from each nation a witness and bring you as a witness against these people; he said: Stop now; and I saw that his eyes were overflowing with tears.
h179.topic: The Prophet weeping at the verse of witnessing

h180.text: Allah said: O My servant, as long as you worship and beg Me, I will forgive you whatever you have done and think nothing of it. O My servant, if you were to meet Me with the earth's fill of sins, yet you did not associate any partner with Me, I would meet you with its fill of forgiveness.

h181.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever obeys me obeys Allah, and whoever disobeys me disobeys Allah; whoever obeys my commander obeys me, and whoever disobeys my commander disobeys me.
h181.topic: Obedience to the Messenger and the ruler

h182.text: May Allah curse those who tattoo and those who have it done, those who pluck their facial hair and those who file their teeth for beauty, altering the creation of Allah. Ibn Mas'ud added: Why should I not curse those whom the Messenger of Allah cursed, when it is in the Book of Allah.

h183.text: 'Umar said: There is nothing I asked the Messenger of Allah about more than the meaning of Kalalah, until he jabbed me in the chest with his finger and said: The verse at the end of Surat an-Nisa should suffice you.

h184.text: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: A Jewish man said to me, 'O Leader of the Believers, there is a verse in your Book which you recite; had it been revealed to us, we would have taken that day as a day of celebration.' I asked which verse, and he recited, 'This day I have perfected your religion for you.' Umar replied, 'By Allah, I know the day and the place where it was revealed to the Messenger of Allah. It was the evening of the Day of Arafah, on a Friday.'
h184.topic: Perfection of the religion at Arafah

h185.text: A woman of the tribe of Makhzum committed theft, and the Quraysh were concerned about her, so they had Usamah bin Zayd, whom the Messenger of Allah loved, speak to him on her behalf. His face changed and he said, 'Do you intercede concerning one of the punishments prescribed by Allah?' Then he addressed the people and said, 'Those before you were destroyed because when a noble person among them stole, they let him go, but when a weak person stole, they carried out the punishment on him. By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad were to steal, I would cut off her hand.'
h185.topic: Equality before the prescribed punishment for theft

h186.text: Eight people from the tribe of Ukl came to the Messenger of Allah and accepted Islam, but the climate of Al-Madinah did not suit them and they fell ill. He sent them out with the herdsman and his camels to drink their milk and urine, and they recovered, but then they killed the herdsman and drove away the camels. The Prophet sent men after them, and when they were captured he had their hands and feet cut off and their eyes branded, and they were left until they died.
h186.topic: Punishment for waging war and spreading corruption

h187.text: Ar-Rabi', the aunt of Anas, broke the tooth of a girl. Her family sought forgiveness but the other party refused, so they came to the Prophet, who ordered retaliation. Anas bin An-Nadr asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, will the tooth of Ar-Rabi' be broken?' He said, 'O Anas, the Book of Allah prescribes retaliation.' Later the girl's family agreed to pardon, and the Messenger of Allah said, 'Among the servants of Allah are those who, if they swear an oath by Allah, He fulfills it for them.'

h188.text: Whoever, when he hears the call to prayer, says, 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and the prayer to be established, grant Muhammad the Wasilah and the excellence, and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him,' will have my intercession permitted for him on the Day of Resurrection.
h188.topic: Supplication after the call to prayer and the Wasilah

h189.text: Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is not able, then with his tongue; and if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith.

h190.text: Aisha said: Whoever tells you that Muhammad concealed any part of what Allah revealed to him has uttered a lie, for Allah says, 'O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord.'
h190.topic: The Prophet conveyed the entire Message

h191.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Every intoxicant is Khamr, and every intoxicant is unlawful. Whoever drinks Khamr and dies while addicted to it, not having repented from it, will not drink it in the Hereafter.

h192.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Five kinds of animals are harmful and may be killed whether in the state of Ihram or not: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse, and the rabid dog.
h192.topic: Animals that may be killed during Ihram

h193.text: The Messenger of Allah gave a speech unlike any I had heard, in which he said, 'If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much.' The Companions covered their faces, weeping. A man asked, 'Who is my father?' He said, 'So-and-so,' and this verse was revealed, 'Ask not about things which, if made plain to you, may cause you trouble.'

h194.text: When the verse was revealed, 'Say: He has the power to send torment on you from above,' the Messenger of Allah said, 'I seek refuge with Your Face.' When it continued, 'or from under your feet,' he again said, 'I seek refuge with Your Face.' When it continued, 'or to cover you with confusion in party strife and make you taste the violence of one another,' he said, 'This is lighter,' or 'easier.'
h194.topic: Seeking refuge from divine torment and discord

h195.text: The Messenger of Allah prayed at length and then said, 'I asked my Lord for three things: I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by drowning, and He granted that to me; I asked Him not to destroy my Ummah by famine, and He granted that to me; and I asked Him not to make them taste the violence of one another, but He did not grant that to me.'
h195.topic: The Prophet's three requests for his Ummah

h196.text: When the verse 'and confuse not their belief with Zulm (wrong)' was revealed, it was hard upon the people, and they said, 'O Messenger of Allah, who among us has not wronged himself?' He said, 'It is not as you understand it. Have you not heard what the righteous servant Luqman said: O my son, join not in worship others with Allah; verily, Shirk is a great wrong indeed.' Thus it refers to Shirk.
h196.topic: The wrong (Zulm) in this verse means Shirk

h197.text: Verily, Allah does not sleep, and it does not befit His majesty that He should sleep. He lowers the scale and raises it. The deeds of the day are raised to Him before the night, and the deeds of the night before the day. His Veil is Light; were He to remove it, the splendor of His Face would burn everything of His creation that His sight reaches.
h197.topic: Allah's Veil of Light and majesty

h198.text: The Prophet said: You may eat whatever causes blood to flow and over which the Name of Allah has been mentioned at the time of slaughtering.

h199.text: The Messenger of Allah said: I was chosen from the best generations of the Children of Adam, generation after generation, until I was sent in the generation in which I am.
h199.topic: The noble lineage of the Prophet

h200.text: The Messenger of Allah said: May Allah curse the Jews. The fats of animals were forbidden to them, yet they melted the fat down, sold it, and consumed its price.
h200.topic: Curse upon those who circumvent what Allah forbade

h201.text: Jibril came to me and gave me the good news that whoever among your followers dies worshipping none alongside Allah will enter Paradise. I asked, 'Even if he stole or committed unlawful intercourse?' He said, 'Even if he stole or committed unlawful intercourse.'
h201.topic: Dying upon Tawhid leads to Paradise

h202.text: The Messenger of Allah drew a line with his hand and said, 'This is Allah's path, leading straight.' Then he drew lines to its right and its left and said, 'These are the other paths; on each path there is a devil calling to it.' Then he recited: 'And verily, this is My straight path, so follow it, and follow not other paths, for they will separate you away from His path.'
h202.topic: The single straight path versus the divergent paths

h203.text: The Messenger of Allah said: The Last Hour will not begin until the sun rises from the west. When the people see that, all of them will believe; but that is when faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before.
h203.topic: Faith will not avail after the sun rises from the west

h204.text: The angels were created from light, Shaytan was created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what was described to you.
h204.topic: Origin of the creation of angels, Iblis and Adam

h205.text: O people! You will be gathered to Allah barefooted, naked and uncircumcised, just as We began the first creation, We shall repeat it; it is a promise binding upon Us, and We shall surely do it.
h205.topic: Mankind raised again as they were first created

h206.text: Every child is born upon the Fitrah; it is only his parents who turn him into a Jew, a Christian or a Zoroastrian.
h206.topic: Every person is born upon the natural disposition

h207.text: Allah said: I created all My servants as monotheists, but the devils came to them and turned them away from their religion, forbidding them what I had made lawful for them.
h207.topic: People created upright then misled by devils

h208.text: While at Al-Hijr, the dwellings of Thamud, the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded the people to pour out the water they had drawn from the wells of Thamud and to feed the dough to their camels. He forbade them from entering the area of those who were punished, saying: Do not enter upon these people who were punished unless you are weeping, for I fear that what befell them may befall you as well.
h208.topic: Caution at the ruins of the punished people of Thamud

h209.text: Do not prefer me above the Prophets. On the Day of Resurrection people will be struck unconscious, and I will be the first to recover, and I will find Musa holding onto a pillar of the Throne. I do not know whether he recovered before me, or he was compensated for his unconsciousness at the mountain of At-Tur.
h209.topic: Musa being unconscious and the rank of the Prophets

h210.text: Allah, the Exalted, has a hundred mercies. With one of them the creation shows mercy to one another, and by it the beasts are tender toward their offspring. He has kept ninety-nine mercies with Him for the Day of Resurrection.

h211.text: During an incident between Abu Bakr and Umar, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Will you not leave my companion to me? I once said, O people, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, and you said, You have lied, but Abu Bakr said, You have spoken the truth.
h211.topic: The Prophet sent as Messenger to all mankind

h212.text: It will be said to a man from the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: If you owned all that is on the earth, would you offer it as ransom? He will say, Yes. Allah will say: I asked of you something less than that while you were still in the loins of Adam, that you associate nothing with Me, but you refused and insisted on associating others with Me.
h212.topic: The covenant taken from the descendants of Adam

h213.text: The Hour will not begin until the sun rises from the west; when it rises and the people see it, they will all believe, but that is when faith will not benefit a soul that had not believed before. The Hour will begin while two men have spread out a garment between them and they will not be able to conclude their sale or fold it; the Hour will begin after a man has milked his animal but will not be able to drink it; the Hour will begin while a man is mending his watering trough but will not water his animals from it; and the Hour will begin while a man has lifted his morsel of food to his mouth but will not eat it.
h213.topic: The suddenness of the Last Hour

h214.text: Shun the seven destructive sins: associating partners with Allah, magic, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except in justice, consuming Riba (usury), consuming an orphan's wealth, fleeing from the battlefield at the time of fighting, and slandering chaste, unaware, believing women.
h214.topic: The seven destructive sins, including fleeing battle

h215.text: Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla was praying when the Prophet called him, and he did not answer until he finished the prayer. The Prophet said: What prevented you from answering me? Has not Allah said, Answer Allah and His Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life? He then said he would teach him the greatest Surah in the Qur'an before leaving, and taught him Al-Fatihah, saying it is the seven oft-repeated verses.
h215.topic: Answering the Messenger's call; the greatest Surah

h216.text: The likeness of the one who upholds Allah's limits and the one who falls into violating them is that of people who drew lots for places on a ship, some on the upper deck and some on the lower. When those below needed water they had to pass those above, so they said, Let us make a hole in our own part. If those above let them do it, all would drown, but if they stopped them, all would be saved.

h217.text: Allah sent down to me two sources of safety for my Ummah: that Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and that Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. When I die, I will leave the seeking of forgiveness with them until the Day of Resurrection.
h217.topic: Two sources of safety from Allah's punishment

h218.text: Whoever does well in his Islam will not be held accountable for what he did during the time of ignorance, but whoever does evil in his Islam will be taken to account for both his former and his latter deeds.
h218.topic: Islam erases prior sins for one who does well

h219.text: I have been commanded to fight the people until they testify that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah. If they say it, they protect their blood and wealth from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah.
h219.topic: Fighting until the testimony of faith is proclaimed

h220.text: While narrating the report of the delegation of Abd al-Qays, the Prophet commanded them with four things and explained belief in Allah as: testifying that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving the Zakah, and faithfully surrendering one-fifth of the war spoils.
h220.topic: Paying the Khumus is part of faith

h221.text: O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for safety; but when you face them, be patient, and know that Paradise lies under the shade of the swords. Then he supplicated: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Mover of the clouds, Defeater of the Confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them.
h221.topic: Patience and steadfastness when meeting the enemy

h222.text: Allah said: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you, so whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.
h222.topic: Allah forbade injustice; deeds are recorded

h223.text: Horses are of three kinds: a source of reward, a means of shelter, and a source of sin. For the one who tethers a horse in the cause of Allah, whatever it eats and drinks, and even its dung and footprints, are recorded as good deeds for him; for the one who keeps it to remain self-sufficient while not forgetting Allah's right concerning it, it is a shelter; and for the one who keeps it out of pride, show, and enmity toward Muslims, it is a burden of sin.
h223.topic: Preparing horses for the cause of Allah

h224.text: The Prophet said in a sermon during his Hajj: The division of time has turned to its original form which was current when Allah created the heavens and the earth. The year is of twelve months, four of which are sacred: three in succession, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab of Mudar which comes between Jumada and Sha'ban. He then asked what day, month, and town it was, and they answered. He said: Verily, your blood, property and honor are sacred to one another like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this month of yours, in this city of yours. You will meet your Lord and He will question you about your actions. Do not revert to misguidance after me by striking the necks of one another.
h224.topic: The twelve months and the four sacred months

h225.text: Abu Bakr said: I said to the Prophet when we were in the cave, 'If any of them looks down at his feet, he will see us.' He said: O Abu Bakr! What do you think about two, with Allah as their third?
h225.topic: Allah's support of the Prophet in the cave

h226.text: The Messenger of Allah was asked about a man who fights out of courage, or out of rage for his honor, or to show off; which of them is in the cause of Allah? The Prophet said: He who fights so that Allah's Word is superior, then he fights in Allah's cause.
h226.topic: Fighting so that Allah's Word is uppermost

h227.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Every man who does not pay the Zakah due on his money, then on the Day of Resurrection his side, forehead and back will be branded with rods made of fire on a Day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until the servants are judged; then he will be shown his destination, either to Paradise or the Fire.
h227.topic: Punishment for hoarding wealth and withholding Zakah

h228.text: The Prophet said: Do not initiate the Salam (greeting) to the Jews and Christians, and if you meet any of them on a road, force him to its narrowest part.
h228.topic: Conduct toward the People of the Scripture

h229.text: Umar said: By Allah, you, O Messenger of Allah, are dearer to me than everything except myself. The Messenger of Allah said: None among you will attain faith until I become dearer to him than even himself. Umar said: Now, by Allah, you are dearer to me than myself. The Messenger of Allah said: Now, O Umar!
h229.topic: Love of the Prophet over all else

h230.text: Allah, the Exalted, will say to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They will say: 'We respond to You, our Lord, and we are at Your service, and all good is in Your Hand.' He will ask: 'Are you pleased?' They will say: 'Why would we not be pleased, O Lord, while You have given us what You have not given any other of Your creation?' He will say: 'Shall I not give you better than that?' They will say: 'O Lord, what is better than that?' He will say: 'I bestow My pleasure upon you and will never afterwards be angry with you.'
h230.topic: Allah's pleasure is the greatest reward in Paradise

h231.text: When Abdullah bin Ubayy died, his son came to the Messenger of Allah and asked for his shirt to shroud his father, and he gave it. He then asked the Prophet to pray over him, and the Messenger of Allah stood to offer the funeral prayer. Umar took hold of his robe and said: Are you going to pray over him when your Lord has forbidden you? He said: Allah has only given me a choice, for He says, 'Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will not forgive them,' and I will ask more than seventy times.
h231.topic: The Prophet and the funeral of the chief hypocrite

h232.text: When Abu Talib was dying, the Prophet went to him and said: O uncle! Say, 'La ilaha illa-llah,' a word by which I will plead for you with Allah. Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah said: O Abu Talib, would you leave the religion of Abdul-Muttalib? Abu Talib said: Rather, I am upon the religion of Abdul-Muttalib. The Prophet said: I will surely seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden to do so.
h232.topic: Seeking forgiveness for the idolaters is prohibited

h233.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Hold on to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man will keep speaking the truth and striving for truth until he is recorded with Allah as truthful. Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man will keep lying and striving for falsehood until he is recorded with Allah as a great liar.

h234.text: The people of Paradise will be inspired to glorify and praise Allah as easily as they breathe.

h235.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Do not pray against yourselves, do not pray against your children, and do not pray against your wealth, lest your supplication coincide with an hour in which Allah grants what is asked, and He answers you.

h236.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: The world is sweet and green, and Allah is going to install you generations after generations in it to see how you act. So safeguard yourselves against the world and against women, for the first trial of the Children of Israel was through women.
h236.topic: The world as a test for successive generations

h237.text: After leading the dawn prayer following a night of rain, the Prophet (peace be upon him) asked his companions if they knew what their Lord had said. They said Allah and His Messenger know best. He said that Allah said: This morning some of My servants became believers in Me and some disbelievers. Whoever said the rain came by the grace and mercy of Allah is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars; and whoever said the rain came due to such and such a star is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.
h237.topic: Attributing rain to Allah versus the stars

h238.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said that he saw in a dream Jibril at his head and Mika'il at his feet, one telling the other to give him a parable. It was said: Listen, may your ear listen, and understand, may your heart understand. Your likeness and the likeness of your Ummah is that of a king who built a house and prepared a banquet in it, then sent a messenger inviting the people to his food. Some accepted and some refused. Allah is the King, the house is Paradise, and you, Muhammad, are the messenger. Whoever responds to you enters Islam, whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats from it.
h238.topic: Parable of the call to the Abode of Peace

h239.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the verse and said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, a caller will announce that Allah has a promise He wishes to fulfill for them. They will ask what it is, saying: Has He not made our scales heavy, made our faces white, and saved us from the Fire? Then Allah will remove the veil and they will look upon Him. By Allah, they will not have been given anything dearer to them than looking at Him.
h239.topic: The believers seeing Allah in Paradise

h240.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) related that his Lord said: O My servants, I have forbidden oppression for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not oppress one another. Until the end of the hadith: O My servants, it is only your deeds that I record for you and then recompense you for, so let whoever finds good praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise blame no one but himself.

h241.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: We are the last, the foremost on the Day of Resurrection; we will be judged before the rest of creation.
h241.topic: This Ummah judged first on the Day of Resurrection

h242.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Among the servants of Allah are people whom the Prophets and the martyrs will consider fortunate. It was asked who they are, so they may be loved. He said: They are people who loved one another for the sake of Allah, without any wealth or kinship between them. Their faces will be light, upon pulpits of light. They will have no fear when people fear, nor will they grieve when people grieve. Then he recited the verse about the friends of Allah having no fear nor grief.

h243.text: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) arrived in Al-Madinah, the Jews were fasting the day of Ashura. He asked what day this was that they were fasting. They said it was the day on which Musa was victorious over Fir'awn. So the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: You have more right to Musa than they, so fast it.
h243.topic: Fasting Ashura, the day Musa was saved from Fir'awn

h244.text: Abu Bakr said, "O Messenger of Allah, your hair has turned gray." The Prophet (peace be upon him) replied, "Surah Hud, Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatasa'alun (An-Naba'), and Idhash-Shamsu Kuwwirat (At-Takwir) have turned my hair gray."
h244.topic: Surah Hud turned the Prophet's hair gray

h245.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Allah was before everything, and His Throne was over the water. He then wrote in the Preserved Tablet mentioning everything."
h245.topic: Allah's Throne was over the water before creation

h246.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said that Allah, the Mighty and Sublime, said, "Spend and I will spend on you." And he said, "Allah's Hand is full, and it is not diminished by spending throughout the night and the day. Have you seen what has been spent since the creation of the heavens and the earth? It does not diminish what is in His Right Hand, and His Throne was over the water; in His Hand is the Scale, and He lowers and raises it."
h246.topic: Allah's spending never diminishes what He has

h247.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Every child is born upon the Fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Magian, just as a calf is born whole. Have you noticed any calves born mutilated?"
h247.topic: Every child is born upon the natural disposition

h248.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said that Allah, the Exalted, says, "Verily, I created My servants Hunafa' (inclined to truth), but the devils came to them and turned them away from their religion. They made unlawful for them what I had made lawful, and they commanded them to associate partners with Me, for which no authority has been revealed."
h248.topic: People created upon truth but misled by devils

h249.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Verily, Allah will draw the believer near and place His shade over him, concealing him from the people, and make him confess his sins, saying, 'Do you recognize this sin? Do you recognize that sin?' until he confesses all of them and thinks he is about to be destroyed. Then Allah will say, 'I concealed them for you in the world, and today I forgive them for you.' As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, the witnesses will say: These are the ones who lied against their Lord."
h249.topic: Allah's private reckoning of the believer

h250.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Verily, Allah gives respite to a wrongdoer until He seizes him, and then he cannot escape." Then he recited, "Such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong."
h250.topic: Allah's respite to the wrongdoer before seizing him

h251.text: Abu Bakr told that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say, "There is no Muslim who commits a sin, then makes Wudu' and prays two units of prayer, except that he will be forgiven for that sin."
h251.topic: Wudu' and two units of prayer expiate sin

h252.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever performs Wudu' like this Wudu' of mine and then prays two units of prayer without speaking to himself during them, he will be forgiven his previous sins."
h252.topic: Wudu' and two units of prayer bring forgiveness

h253.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Paradise and the Hellfire debated. Paradise said, 'None enters me except the weak and lowly of the people.' The Hellfire said, 'I have the haughty and arrogant.' Allah said to Paradise, 'You are My mercy; through you I show mercy to whom I will,' and to the Hellfire, 'You are My torment; through you I take vengeance on whom I will. Each of you shall have its fill.' Paradise will still have room until Allah creates more beings to dwell in it, while the Hellfire keeps saying, 'Are there any more?' until the Lord places His Foot upon it, and it says, 'Enough, enough, by Your might!'"
h253.topic: Paradise and Hellfire each filled by Allah's will

h254.text: Allah the Exalted said: 'If My slave intends to perform a good deed, then record it for him as one good deed; if he performs it, then record it for him multiplied ten times. If he intends to commit an evil act but does not commit it, then record it for him as one good deed, for he left it only for My sake. But if he commits it, then write it as one evil deed.'
h254.topic: Reward for intending good and restraining from evil

h255.text: Allah will give shade to seven on the Day when there will be no shade but His: a just ruler, a youth who grew up worshipping Allah, a man whose heart is attached to the Masjid, two men who love each other for Allah's sake and meet and part on that basis, a man who gives charity so secretly that his left hand does not know what his right hand spent, a man who is called by a charming woman of noble birth to illicit intercourse but says 'I fear Allah,' and a man who remembers Allah in seclusion so that his eyes overflow with tears.
h255.topic: The seven whom Allah will shade, including one who fears Allah and refuses seduction

h257.text: The Messenger of Allah said: 'We are more liable to be in doubt than Ibrahim when he said, "My Lord! Show me how You give life to the dead." And may Allah send His mercy upon Lut; he wished to have powerful support. And if I were to stay in prison as long as Yusuf did, I would have accepted the offer (to be released).'
h257.topic: The Prophet's praise of Yusuf's patience in prison

h258.text: While he was dying, the Messenger of Allah raised his finger and said three times: 'O Allah, to Ar-Rafiq Al-A'la (the highest company in Paradise).'
h258.topic: The Prophet's supplication at the time of death

h259.text: I asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, what is the greatest sin?' He said: 'That you set up a rival to Allah while He alone created you.'
h259.topic: The greatest sin is associating partners with Allah

h260.text: The Messenger of Allah said: 'Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed Shirk.'
h260.topic: Swearing by other than Allah is a form of Shirk

h261.text: The Messenger of Allah said: 'Verily, incantations, amulets and love-charms are Shirk.'
h261.topic: Charms and amulets are a hidden form of Shirk

h262.text: The Messenger of Allah said: 'The dream is tied to a bird's leg as long as it is not interpreted; once it is interpreted, it comes to pass.'
h262.topic: A dream takes effect once it is interpreted

h263.text: The matter of the creation of one of you is put together in the womb of his mother in forty days, then he becomes a clot of thick blood for a similar period, then a piece of flesh for a similar period. Then Allah sends an angel who is ordered to write four things: his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed.
h263.topic: Stages of creation in the womb and what is decreed

h264.text: The keys of the unseen are five; none knows them but Allah. None knows what will happen tomorrow except Allah; none knows what is in the wombs except Allah; none knows when it will rain except Allah; no soul knows in what land it will die; and none knows when the Hour will begin except Allah.
h264.topic: The five keys of the unseen known only to Allah

h265.text: There is no one among you except that a companion from the jinn and a companion from the angels have been appointed over him. They asked, 'And you too, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'And me too, except that Allah has helped me against him, so he orders me only to do good.'
h265.topic: The angelic and jinn companions appointed over every person

h266.text: The Messenger of Allah used to say upon hearing thunder and thunderbolts: 'O Allah, do not kill us with Your anger, nor destroy us with Your torment, and grant us well-being before that.'

h267.text: Your Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, said: 'Had My servants obeyed Me, I would have given them rain by night and the sun by day, and I would not have made them hear the sound of thunder.'
h267.topic: Obedience would have spared people the warning of thunder

h268.text: The example of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain falling on the earth. Some of it was fertile soil that absorbed the water and brought forth much vegetation and grass. Another portion was hard and held the water, so Allah benefited people by it; they drank, watered their animals, and irrigated. And another portion was barren land that neither held water nor brought forth vegetation. That is the example of one who comprehends the religion of Allah and benefits from what Allah sent me with, so he learns and teaches; and the example of one who pays it no heed and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I was sent.
h268.topic: Parable of guidance falling on different hearts like rain on land

h269.text: My example and your example is like that of a man who kindled a fire. When it illuminated all around him, moths and insects began falling into it as they do, and he tried to hold them back, but they overwhelmed him and plunged in. That is my example and yours: I am holding you back by your waists from the Fire, saying, 'Keep away from the Fire,' yet you overwhelm me and plunge into it.
h269.topic: The Prophet holding people back from the Fire

h270.text: The life of this world compared to the Hereafter is only like one of you dipping this finger of his into the sea; let him consider what it brings back.
h270.topic: The triviality of this world next to the Hereafter

h271.text: There is a tree in Paradise so vast that a rider would travel in its shade for a hundred years and not pass it.
h271.topic: The vastness of the trees of Paradise

h272.text: O My servants, if the first and the last of you, the humans and the jinn among you, were to stand in one place and ask of Me, and I gave every person what he asked, that would not decrease what I possess except as a needle decreases the sea when dipped into it.
h272.topic: The limitless bounty and dominion of Allah

h273.text: I have been given five things which were not given to anyone before me: I have been made victorious through awe (cast into my enemies) for a distance of one month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification; the war booty has been made lawful for me, and it was not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given the right of intercession; and every Prophet used to be sent to his own people only, but I have been sent to all mankind.
h273.topic: Five things granted to the Prophet

h274.text: O My servants, if the first and the last of you, the men and the jinn among you, had the heart of the most pious man among you, that would not increase My kingdom in the least. O My servants, if the first and the last of you, the men and the jinn among you, had the heart of the most wicked man among you, that would not decrease My kingdom in the least. O My servants, if the first and the last of you, the men and the jinn among you, stood in one place and each asked Me, and I gave every one what he asked, that would not decrease what I have any more than a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it.
h274.topic: Allah is free of all need

h275.text: The Messenger of Allah asked: Tell me about a tree that resembles the Muslim, whose leaves do not fall in summer or winter and which gives its fruit at all times by the leave of its Lord. Ibn Umar said: I thought of the date palm but felt too shy to speak when I saw that Abu Bakr and Umar were silent. When the people did not answer, the Messenger of Allah said: It is the date palm tree.
h275.topic: The good word likened to a date palm

h276.text: When the Muslim is questioned in the grave, he will testify that there is no deity worthy of worship but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah. That is the meaning of Allah's statement, 'Allah will keep firm those who believe, with the word that stands firm in this world and in the Hereafter.'
h276.topic: Steadfastness when questioned in the grave

h277.text: When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions depart, while he hears the sound of their sandals, two angels come to him, sit him up, and ask him: What did you used to say about this man? As for the believer, he says: I bear witness that he is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. He is then told: Look at your place in the Fire; Allah has replaced it for you with a place in Paradise. So he sees both of them.
h277.topic: The believer's questioning in the grave

h279.text: On the Day of Resurrection, the people will be gathered on a white, flat earth like a loaf of pure bread, having no landmark for anyone.
h279.topic: The earth changed on the Day of Resurrection

h280.text: Aisha said: I was the first of all people to ask the Messenger of Allah about this verse, 'On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth and so will be the heavens.' I said: O Messenger of Allah, where will the people be then? He said: On the Sirat (the Bridge).
h280.topic: Where people will be when the earth is changed

h281.text: Four matters from the time of ignorance will remain among my Ummah, which they will not abandon: boasting about lineage, slandering ancestry, seeking rain by the stars, and wailing over the dead. The wailing woman, if she does not repent before her death, will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a shirt of mange.

h282.text: When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His Word, like a chain striking a smooth rock. When the fright leaves their hearts, they ask one another, 'What did your Lord say?' They reply, 'The truth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.' Then the eavesdropping devils, standing one above another, snatch what they hear; sometimes a flaming fire strikes the eavesdropper before he can pass it on, and sometimes he conveys it to the one below him, who carries it to a sorcerer or fortune-teller, who then mixes it with a hundred lies.

h283.text: Among the people of Hell are those whom the Fire will swallow up to the ankles, and those whom it will swallow up to the waist, and those whom it will swallow up to the collarbone.
h283.topic: Levels of the people of the Fire

h284.text: The believers will be removed from the Fire and detained on a bridge between Paradise and Hell. Then they will be requited for the wrongs they committed against one another in this world, until they are cleansed and purified, and then permission will be given to them to enter Paradise.

h285.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) passed by me while I was praying and called me, but I did not come until I had finished. When I came he asked, 'What stopped you from coming to me?' I said, 'I was praying.' He said, 'Did not Allah say: O you who believe! Answer Allah and His Messenger when he calls you?' Then he said, 'Shall I not teach you the most magnificent Surah in the Qur'an before I leave the Masjid?' When he was about to leave I reminded him, and he said, 'Al-Hamdu Lillahi Rabbil-Alamin (Al-Fatihah); it is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Grand Qur'an which I have been given.'
h285.topic: Al-Fatihah is the seven oft-repeated verses

h286.text: Umm al-Qur'an (the Mother of the Qur'an) is the seven oft-repeated verses and the Grand Qur'an.

h287.text: My parable and that with which Allah has sent me is like a man who came to his people and said, 'O people, I have seen the army with my own eyes, and I am a naked warner, so flee, flee!' A group of his people obeyed him and set off by night and were saved, while another group disbelieved him and stayed where they were, so the army came upon them in the morning and destroyed them. That is the parable of the one who obeys me and follows what I brought, and of the one who disobeys me and rejects the truth I brought.
h287.topic: Parable of the Prophet as a warner

h288.text: Allah said: O son of Adam, do not be too weak to pray four Rak'at at the beginning of the day, and I will suffice you for the rest of it.
h288.topic: Four Rak'at at the start of the day

h289.text: Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then lying on your side.

h290.text: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) entered upon Uthman bin Maz'un after he had died, Umm al-Ala said, 'May Allah's mercy be upon you, Abu As-Sa'ib; my testimony over you is that Allah has honored you.' He said, 'How do you know that Allah has honored him?' She said, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah! If not him, then who?' He said, 'As for him, death has come to him, and I hope for good for him.'
h290.topic: Not testifying to the unseen reward of the dead

h292.text: Allah, may He be exalted, says: 'O son of Adam, how could you be more powerful than Me when I created you from something like this; and when I have fashioned you perfectly and made you complete, you walk wearing your two garments and the earth makes a sound beneath your feet. You collect wealth and withhold it, until when the soul reaches the throat you say, I want to give in charity, but it is too late for charity.'
h292.topic: Man created from a lowly drop

h293.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) forbade us to eat the meat of domestic donkeys, but he allowed us to eat the meat of horses.

h294.text: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) and said, 'My brother is suffering from diarrhea.' He said, 'Give him honey to drink.' The man did so but returned saying it only made him worse. The Prophet (peace be upon him) repeated, 'Go and give him honey to drink,' and again the man said it made him worse. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Allah speaks the truth and your brother's stomach is lying. Go and give him honey to drink.' So he gave him honey and he recovered.

h295.text: Healing is to be found in three things: the cut made by the cupper, drinking honey, or branding with fire (cauterizing); but I have forbidden my Ummah to use branding.

h297.text: Allah says: 'Whoever takes a friend of Mine as an enemy, I declare war on him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than the duties I have enjoined upon him, and My servant keeps drawing near to Me with voluntary deeds until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. Were he to ask Me, I would give him; were he to seek refuge in Me, I would grant him refuge. I do not hesitate over anything I do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he hates death and I hate to grieve him, yet it must come to him.'
h297.topic: Allah's love for His devoted servant

h298.text: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was sitting with Uthman bin Maz'un, he gazed at the sky and then lowered his gaze, as if listening to something being said to him. He then explained that a messenger from Allah had just come to him and conveyed the words, 'Verily, Allah orders justice and kindness, and giving to relatives, and He forbids immoral sins, evil, and tyranny.'
h298.topic: The revelation of the verse of justice and kindness

h299.text: There is no oath of alliance in Islam, and any oath of alliance made during the time of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) is only made stronger by Islam.

h300.text: He who submits to Allah has succeeded, is given sufficient provision, and is made content by Allah with what He has given him.

h301.text: When the Quraysh did not believe that I had been taken on the Night Journey to Bayt Al-Maqdis, I stood up in Al-Hijr and Allah displayed Bayt Al-Maqdis before me, so I told them about its features while I was looking at it.
h301.topic: The Prophet shown Jerusalem after Quraysh denied the Night Journey

h302.text: Al-Buraq was brought to me, a white animal larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, whose stride reached as far as it could see. I rode it to Bayt Al-Maqdis and tethered it where the Prophets tether their animals, and I prayed two units there. Then I was taken up through the heavens, where I met Adam, then Yahya and Isa, then Yusuf, then Idris, then Harun, then Musa, then Ibrahim leaning against the Much-Frequented House. Then fifty prayers each day were enjoined upon me, and I kept returning to my Lord at Musa's urging until they were reduced to five, equal in reward to fifty.
h302.topic: The Night Journey and Ascension and the enjoining of the prayers

h303.text: Every newborn is born in a state of Fitrah (the natural disposition), then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian or a Magian, just as animals produce whole offspring; do you see any born mutilated?
h303.topic: Every child is born upon the natural disposition

h304.text: He is doomed, he is doomed, he is doomed: the man whose parents, one or both of them, reach old age while he is alive, and he does not enter Paradise (through serving them).
h304.topic: Honoring one's parents in their old age

h305.text: I asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, which sin is the worst?' He said, 'To set up a rival to Allah when He created you.' I asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'To kill your child for fear that he will eat with you.' I asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'To commit adultery with your neighbor's wife.'

h306.text: The blood of a Muslim who testifies that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah is not lawful to shed except in three cases: a life for a life, a married person who commits adultery, and one who forsakes his religion and abandons the community.
h306.topic: When the killing of a Muslim is lawful

h307.text: None of you should point at his brother with a weapon, for he does not know whether Shaytan may cause him to strike him with it, and thus he would fall into a pit of the Fire.
h307.topic: Prohibition of pointing a weapon at a Muslim

h308.text: The angels of the night and the angels of the day come amongst you in succession, and they meet at the Fajr prayer and the Asr prayer. Then those who stayed with you ascend, and their Lord asks them, though He knows best about you, 'How did you leave My servants?' They say, 'We came to them while they were praying and we left them while they were praying.'
h308.topic: The angels witnessing the dawn prayer

h309.text: I will be the master of mankind on the Day of Resurrection. Allah will gather the first and the last, and when the people's distress becomes unbearable they will seek someone to intercede, going to Adam, then Nuh, then Ibrahim, then Musa, then Isa, each excusing himself, until they come to me. I will prostrate beneath the Throne and Allah will inspire me with praises, then it will be said, 'Raise your head, ask and it will be granted, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' This is the praised station (Al-Maqam Al-Mahmud).
h309.topic: The Great Intercession and the Praised Station
