h310.text: While I was walking with the Prophet (peace be upon him) on a farm, and he was leaning on a palm-leaf stalk, some Jews passed by and asked him about the spirit (the Ruh). He remained silent and I realized he was receiving revelation. Then he recited: 'They ask you concerning the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the affair of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.'

h311.text: Whoever memorizes ten Ayat from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal.
h311.topic: Protection from the Dajjal by reciting Al-Kahf

h313.text: Sulayman bin Dawud said: Tonight I will go around to seventy women so that each one of them will give birth to a son who will fight for the sake of Allah. It was said to him, Say: If Allah wills, but he did not say it. He went around to the women but none of them gave birth except for one who gave birth to a half-formed child. The Prophet said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, had he said, If Allah wills, he would not have broken his oath, and that would have helped him to attain what he wanted.
h313.topic: Saying 'If Allah wills' for future intentions

h314.text: There was a group of six of us with the Prophet. The idolators said, Tell these people to leave so they will not offend us. Allah's Messenger thought to himself about whatever Allah willed he should think about, then Allah revealed: And turn not away those who invoke their Lord, morning and afternoon.
h314.topic: Keeping company with the weak believers

h315.text: Every traitor will have a banner on the Day of Resurrection by which he will be known. On the Day of Resurrection, for every traitor a banner will be erected by his backside, and it will be said, This is the betrayer of so-and-so the son of so-and-so.
h315.topic: Every traitor will be exposed on the Day of Resurrection

h316.text: The angels were created from light, Iblis was created from smokeless fire, and Adam was created from that which has been described to you.
h316.topic: The creation of angels, Iblis and Adam

h317.text: Musa got up to deliver a speech before the Children of Israel and he was asked, Who is the most learned person among the people? Musa replied, I am. Allah rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Allah, so Allah revealed to him that at the junction of the two seas there was a servant of His more learned than him. Musa asked how he could meet him, and was told to take a fish in a vessel and that where he lost the fish he would find him. Musa set out with his boy-servant Yusha' bin Nun, and where the fish made its way into the sea he found Al-Khidr, and he followed him to learn from his knowledge.
h317.topic: The story of Musa and Al-Khidr

h319.text: He was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a barren patch of withered vegetation and it turned green beneath him.
h319.topic: Why Al-Khidr was given his name

h320.text: La ilaha illallah! Woe to the Arabs from the evil that has approached. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj like this, and he made a circle with his index finger and thumb. He was asked, Will we be destroyed even though there will be righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases.
h320.topic: The opening of the barrier of Ya'juj and Ma'juj

h321.text: Whoever testifies that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah alone, having no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that 'Isa was Allah's servant and Messenger and His word which He cast upon Maryam and a spirit from Him, and that Paradise and Hell are real, Allah will admit him into Paradise regardless of his deeds.
h321.topic: Testifying that 'Isa is Allah's servant and Messenger

h322.text: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, death will be brought in the form of a handsome ram and placed between Paradise and the Fire. It will be said, 'O people of Paradise, do you know what this is?' They will look and say, 'Yes, this is death.' It will be said, 'O people of the Fire, do you know what this is?' They will look and say, 'Yes, this is death.' Then the order will be given and it will be slaughtered, and it will be said, 'O people of Paradise, eternity and no more death; O people of the Fire, eternity and no more death.'
h322.topic: The slaughter of death between Paradise and the Fire

h323.text: May Allah have mercy upon a man who gets up at night to pray and wakes his wife, and if she refuses, sprinkles water on her face. May Allah have mercy upon a woman who gets up at night to pray and wakes her husband, and if he refuses, sprinkles water on his face.
h323.topic: Enjoining one's family to night prayer

h324.text: The first group to enter Paradise will have forms like the moon on the night when it is full. They will not spit, nor blow their noses, nor relieve themselves therein. Their vessels and combs will be of gold and silver, their censers of aloeswood, and their sweat will be musk. Each of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shins will be visible through the flesh due to their beauty. There will be no disputes or hatred among them; their hearts will be as the heart of one man, glorifying Allah morning and evening.
h324.topic: The first group to enter Paradise

h325.text: The martyrs will be upon the banks of a river by the gates of Paradise, under a green dome, and their sustenance will be brought out to them from Paradise morning and evening.
h325.topic: The sustenance of the martyrs morning and evening

h326.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Jibril, 'What prevents you from visiting us more than you do?' Then this verse was revealed: 'And we descend not except by the command of your Lord.'
h326.topic: The angels descend only by Allah's command

h327.text: Allah said: The son of Adam denies Me, though he has no right to deny Me, and he insults Me, though he has no right to insult Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his saying that I will not resurrect him as I created him the first time, yet the second creation is not harder for Me than the first. As for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a son, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Me.
h327.topic: Allah's denial of resurrection and of a son being ascribed to Him

h328.text: No Muslim who has had three of his children die will be touched by the Fire, except for the fulfillment of the oath.
h328.topic: Whoever loses three children is spared the Fire

h329.text: There is no one more patient with harmful words he hears than Allah: partners are ascribed to Him and a son is attributed to Him, while He is the One who gives them good health, protects them, and provides for them.
h329.topic: Allah's forbearance toward those who ascribe a son to Him

h330.text: When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says, 'I love so-and-so, so love him.' Then Jibril loves him and calls out to the dwellers of the heavens, 'Allah loves so-and-so, so love him,' and the dwellers of the heavens love him; then acceptance is placed for him on the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He calls Jibril and says, 'I hate so-and-so, so hate him,' and Jibril hates him and calls out to the dwellers of the heavens to hate him, and then hatred for him is placed on the earth.
h330.topic: Allah placing love for the righteous on earth

h331.text: Whomever Allah wants good for, He gives him the understanding of the religion.
h331.topic: Understanding of religion is a sign of Allah's good for a person

h332.text: Whoever slept past the prayer, or forgot it, then his expiation is that he prays it when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it other than that.
h332.topic: Making up a missed or forgotten prayer

h333.text: Adam and Musa met, and Musa said, 'You are the one who made things difficult for mankind and caused them to be evicted from Paradise.' Adam said, 'Are you the one whom Allah chose for His Message, selected for Himself, and to whom He revealed the Tawrah? Are you blaming me for a matter that Allah preordained upon me before He created me?' So Adam defeated Musa's argument.
h333.topic: Adam and Musa dispute over destiny

h334.text: The dwellers of Hellfire who deserve it will neither die in it nor live. Rather they are a people punished by the Fire for their sins; it will gradually consume them until they become burnt coals. Then intercession will be allowed, and they will be brought out group by group and spread upon the rivers of Paradise, and it will be said, 'O people of Paradise, pour water over them.' Then they will grow like a seed grows on the banks of a flowing river.
h334.topic: Sinful believers brought out of Hell

h335.text: When the Messenger of Allah came to Al-Madinah he found the Jews fasting the day of Ashura. He asked them about it and they said, 'This is the day Allah gave Musa victory over Fir'awn.' So the Prophet said, 'We have more right to Musa than they do,' and he fasted it.

h336.text: The Messenger of Allah used to strive hard to retain the revelation, moving his tongue rapidly to recite it as it came down. So Allah revealed, 'Move not your tongue to make haste with it; it is for Us to collect it and to give you the ability to recite it,' assuring him that it would be gathered in his chest and he would recite it without forgetting any of it.
h336.topic: Not hastening with the recitation of revelation

h337.text: You will see your Lord just as you see this full moon, and you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to miss a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting, then do so.
h337.topic: Seeing Allah and guarding the Fajr and Asr prayers

h338.text: Anyone who prays before the rising of the sun and before its setting will never enter the Hellfire.
h338.topic: Reward for guarding the Fajr and Asr prayers

h339.text: Umar entered upon the Prophet and saw him lying on a sandy straw mat that left marks on his side, with almost nothing in the room, and Umar's eyes filled with tears. He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, Kisra and Caesar live in luxury, yet you are the chosen Friend of Allah.' The Prophet said, 'Do you have doubt, O son of Al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things have been hastened for them in the life of this world.'
h339.topic: The Prophet's abstinence from worldly luxury

h340.text: Paradise has one hundred levels, and between each level is a distance like that between the sky and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest of them; from it spring the four rivers of Paradise and above it is the Throne. So when you ask Allah, ask Him for Al-Firdaws.
h340.topic: The levels of Paradise and Al-Firdaws

h341.text: Two words are light on the tongue, heavy in the Balance and beloved to the Most Gracious: 'Subhan Allahi wa bi hamdihi, Subhan Allahil 'Azim' (Glory and praise be to Allah; Glory be to Allah the Almighty).

h342.text: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, did not tell lies except on three occasions: two of them for the sake of Allah, when he said 'Nay, this one, the biggest of them did it,' and when he said 'Verily, I am sick'; and once concerning his wife Sarah, when he told a tyrant that she was his sister.
h342.topic: Ibrahim and the breaking of the idols

h343.text: If the judge exercises his judgement, studies the case and reaches the correct conclusion, he will have two rewards; and if he exercises his judgement, studies the case and reaches the wrong conclusion, he will have one reward.
h343.topic: The reward of the judge who strives

h344.text: Two women each had a son, and a wolf came and took one of the children. They referred their dispute to Dawud, who ruled that the remaining child belonged to the older woman. Then Sulayman called them and said, 'Bring me a knife and I will divide him between you.' The younger woman said, 'May Allah have mercy on you! He is her child; do not cut him.' So Sulayman ruled that the child belonged to the younger woman.

h345.text: The supplication of Dhun-Nun when he was in the belly of the fish was: 'There is no god but You, Glorified be You; truly I have been of the wrongdoers.' No Muslim ever supplicates his Lord with these words for anything but He answers his prayer.

h346.text: Allah will send the Messiah 'Isa son of Maryam, who will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, and he will pursue and kill the Dajjal at the eastern gate of Ludd. Then Allah will let loose Ya'juj and Ma'juj, who will swoop down from every height; 'Isa and his companions will beseech Allah, who will send a worm into the necks of Ya'juj and Ma'juj so that they all perish, after which Allah will purify and bless the earth.
h346.topic: The Dajjal and the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj

h347.text: 'Isa son of Maryam will certainly come to this House (the Ka'bah) and perform Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj.
h347.topic: 'Isa performing Hajj after Ya'juj and Ma'juj

h348.text: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will seize the earth, and the heavens will be in His Right Hand.
h348.topic: The heavens rolled up on the Day of Resurrection

h349.text: You will be gathered before Allah barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, just as We began the first creation, so We shall repeat it.
h349.topic: The gathering on the Day of Resurrection

h350.text: I was not sent as one who curses; rather, I was sent only as a mercy.
h350.topic: The Prophet as a mercy to the worlds

h351.text: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will call Adam and command him to send forth from his progeny those destined for the Fire. Adam will ask how many, and Allah will say: from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine. At that the pregnant will drop their loads and children will turn grey. The Prophet then said that in comparison to the rest of mankind his Ummah would be like a black hair on a white bull, and expressed hope they would be a quarter, then a third, then half of the people of Paradise.
h351.topic: Terror of the Day of Resurrection

h352.text: The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then an angel is sent to him and is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his deeds, his lifespan, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. Then the soul is breathed into him.
h352.topic: Stages of human creation in the womb

h353.text: The Prophet asked Abu Dharr if he knew where the sun goes. Abu Dharr said Allah and His Messenger know best. The Prophet said that it goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then awaits permission, and soon it will be told to return the way it came.

h354.text: When the son of Adam recites a verse of prostration and prostrates, the Shaytan withdraws weeping and says: Woe to me! The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate and he prostrated, so Paradise is his; and I was commanded to prostrate and I refused, so the Fire is mine.
h354.topic: Merit of the prostration of recitation

h355.text: Abu Dharr asked which mosque was built first. The Prophet said: Al-Masjid al-Haram. He asked which next, and the Prophet said: Bayt al-Maqdis. He asked how long between them, and the Prophet said: forty years.
h355.topic: The first house of worship established

h356.text: The Prophet was asked whether there are any deeds more virtuous than deeds done during these ten days. He said no, not even Jihad in the cause of Allah, except for a man who goes out risking himself and his wealth and returns with nothing.
h356.topic: Virtue of the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah

h357.text: The Prophet was asked about fasting on the Day of 'Arafah and said: I hope from Allah that it will be an expiation for the year before it and the year after it.

h358.text: The Prophet said: Shall I not tell you of the worst of the major sins? They said yes. He said: associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to one's parents. He was reclining, then he sat up and said: and indeed false speech and false testimony, and he kept repeating it until they wished he would stop.
h358.topic: False testimony among the gravest sins

h359.text: The Prophet said: Allah grants respite to the wrongdoer, but when He seizes him He does not let him escape. Then he recited the verse: Such is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are doing wrong; His seizure is painful and severe.
h359.topic: Allah's respite then seizure of wrongdoers

h360.text: Allah says: Who does greater wrong than one who sets out to create something like My creation? Let them create an ant, or let them create a grain of barley.

h361.text: The creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a Nutfah, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then a little lump of flesh for a similar period. Then the angel is sent to him and breathes the soul into him, and is commanded with four matters: to write down his provision, his life-span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed.
h361.topic: Stages of human creation and the decree

h362.text: If you ask Allah for Paradise, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the highest part of Paradise and the middle of Paradise, and from it spring the rivers of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.

h363.text: Ibn Mas'ud asked the Messenger of Allah which deed is most beloved to Allah. He said, 'Prayer at its appointed time.' He asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'Kindness to one's parents.' He asked, 'Then what?' He said, 'Jihad in the way of Allah.'
h363.topic: The most beloved deeds to Allah

h364.text: Fragrance and women have been made dear to me, and the coolness of my eye has been placed in the prayer.
h364.topic: Prayer as the delight of the Prophet's eye

h365.text: O people, Allah is Tayyib (good and pure) and accepts only that which is Tayyib. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the Messengers. Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky saying 'O Lord, O Lord,' while his food, drink and clothing are unlawful and he is nourished by what is unlawful, so how can his supplication be answered?
h365.source: Sahih Muslim, Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Musnad Ahmad
h365.topic: Allah accepts only what is pure and lawful

isnad.name: Sahih Muslim, Jami' at-Tirmidhi and Musnad Ahmad

h366.text: Allah created Adam from a handful which He took from all of the earth, so the sons of Adam came forth in accordance with it: red, white and black and in between, evil and good and in between.
h366.source: Musnad Ahmad, Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi
h366.topic: The creation of Adam from the dust of the earth

isnad.name: Musnad Ahmad, Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi

h367.text: Aisha asked whether 'those who give what they give with their hearts full of fear' are those who steal, commit adultery and drink alcohol while fearing Allah. The Messenger of Allah said, 'No, O daughter of As-Siddiq. They are those who pray, fast and give in charity while fearing that it will not be accepted from them.'
h367.topic: Doing good deeds while fearing they may not be accepted

h368.text: There is no one among you but he has two abodes: an abode in Paradise and an abode in the Fire. If he dies and enters the Fire, the people of Paradise will inherit his abode.
h368.topic: The believers inheriting the abodes of the people of the Fire

h369.text: Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it comes from a blessed tree.
h369.topic: The blessing of the olive tree and its oil

h370.text: On the Day of Resurrection some of the Muslims will come with sins like mountains, but Allah will forgive them and place that burden upon the Jews and Christians.

h371.text: Two bedouins came to the Prophet (peace be upon him); one said his son had committed adultery with the other man's wife and that he had paid a ransom of one hundred sheep and a slave-girl. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will judge between you both according to the Book of Allah. Take back the slave-girl and the sheep; your son is to be given one hundred stripes and banished for one year. And O Unays, go to this man's wife, and if she confesses, then stone her." She confessed, and she was stoned.
h371.topic: Punishment for adultery: flogging and banishment

h372.text: Hilal bin Umayyah accused his wife before the Prophet (peace be upon him) of adultery with Sharik bin Sahma'. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Bring evidence, or the punishment will be carried out on your back." After the verses of Li'an were revealed, he had them both swear: Hilal testified four times by Allah that he was truthful and a fifth time invoking Allah's curse upon himself if he lied; his wife testified four times that he lied and a fifth time invoking Allah's wrath upon herself if he was truthful. The Prophet (peace be upon him) then separated them.
h372.topic: The procedure of Li'an between spouses

h373.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Shun the seven destructive sins." They asked, "What are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah; magic; killing a soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right; consuming Riba; consuming the property of the orphan; fleeing on the day of battle; and accusing chaste, believing women who never even think of anything touching their chastity."

h374.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) smiled and said, "Do you know why I am smiling?" We said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Because of the way a person will dispute with his Lord. He will say, 'O Lord, did You not protect me from injustice?' Allah will say, 'Of course.' The man will say, 'I will not accept any witness against me except myself.' Allah will say, 'You are sufficient as a witness against yourself today.' Then his mouth will be sealed and his limbs will be told to speak, and they will speak of his deeds."
h374.topic: The limbs testifying on the Day of Resurrection

h375.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The son of Adam has his share of Zina decreed for him, and he will inevitably commit it. The Zina of the eyes is looking; the Zina of the tongue is speaking; the Zina of the ears is listening; the Zina of the hands is striking; and the Zina of the feet is walking. The soul wishes and desires, and the private parts confirm that or deny it."
h375.topic: Guarding the gaze and the Zina of the limbs

h376.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "O young men, whoever among you can afford to marry, let him marry, for it is more effective in lowering the gaze and protecting the private parts. And whoever cannot, let him fast, for it will be a shield for him."

h377.text: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) got up to pray at night, he would say: "O Allah, to You be praise, You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. To You be praise, You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them."
h377.topic: Supplication affirming Allah as the Light

h378.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever builds a mosque seeking the Face of Allah, Allah will build for him something similar to it in Paradise."

h379.text: While Mu'adh was riding behind the Prophet (peace be upon him), he said: "O Mu'adh, do you know the right that Allah has over His servants?" Mu'adh said, "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The right that Allah has over His servants is that they should worship Him and not associate anything with Him." Then he asked, "Do you know the right the servants have over Allah if they do that?" He said: "That He will not punish them."
h379.topic: The right of Allah: worship without associating partners

h380.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "The parable of me and you is that of a man who kindled a fire, and when it lit up everything around him, moths and creatures began falling into it while he tried to hold them back, but they overwhelmed him and fell in. That is the parable of me and you: I am seizing you by your waists to keep you from the Fire, saying 'Come away from the Fire,' but you overpower me and plunge into it."
h380.topic: The Prophet warning his Ummah from the Fire

h381.text: The Prophet was asked which sin is the most serious. He said: 'That you appoint a rival to Allah when He has created you.' He was asked, 'Then what?' He said: 'That you kill your child for fear that he may eat with you.' He was asked, 'Then what?' He said: 'That you commit adultery with your neighbor's wife.'

h382.text: I know the last person who will be brought forth from Hell and the last person who will enter Paradise. A man will be brought and it will be said, 'Take away his major sins and ask him about his minor sins.' He will be told, 'On such and such a day you did such and such,' and he will affirm it, unable to deny anything. Then it will be said, 'For every evil deed you now have one good merit.' He will say, 'O Lord, I did things that I do not see here.' And the Messenger of Allah smiled so broadly that his molars could be seen.
h382.topic: Sins changed into good deeds for the repentant

h383.text: It was said, 'O Messenger of Allah, can we perform Wudu' with the water of the well of Buda'ah, for it is a well into which rubbish and the flesh of dogs are thrown?' He said: 'Water is pure and nothing makes it impure.'

h385.text: The Messenger of Allah said three times: 'Shall I not tell you of the greatest of major sins?' We said, 'Of course, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Associating others in worship with Allah, and disobeying one's parents.' He was lying down, then he sat up and added: 'Beware false speech, and bearing witness to falsehood,' and he kept repeating it until we wished he would stop.

h386.text: When a son of Adam dies, his deeds cease apart from three: a righteous child who will pray for him, knowledge from which others may benefit after him, or ongoing charity.

h387.text: Allah says: 'I will test you and test others by means of you.'
h387.topic: People as a trial for one another

h388.text: One morning after a night's rain the Messenger of Allah said to his Companions: 'Do you know what your Lord says?' They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'He says: This morning some of My servants became believers in Me and some became disbelievers. As for the one who said, We have been given rain by the mercy and grace of Allah, he is a believer in Me and a disbeliever in the stars. As for the one who said, We have been given rain by such and such a star, he is a disbeliever in Me and a believer in the stars.'
h388.topic: Attributing rain to Allah versus the stars

h389.text: Ibrahim will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and there will be dust and darkness on Azar's face. Ibrahim will say to him: 'Did I not tell you not to disobey me?' His father will say: 'Today I will not disobey you.' Ibrahim will say: 'O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day when they are resurrected, but what disgrace could be greater than seeing my father in this state?' Allah will say: 'I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.'
h389.topic: Ibrahim and his father on the Day of Resurrection

h390.text: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet climbed As-Safa and called out to the clans of Quraysh, saying: 'O Bani Abd Al-Muttalib, O Bani Fihr, O Bani Lu'ayy! What do you think, if I told you there was a cavalry at the foot of this mountain coming to attack you, would you believe me?' They said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Then I warn you of a great punishment that is close at hand.' Abu Lahab said: 'May you perish! You only called us to tell us this?' Then Allah revealed: 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab.'
h390.topic: Warning the near kindred at As-Safa

h391.text: When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah stood up and said: 'O Fatimah daughter of Muhammad, O Safiyyah daughter of Abd Al-Muttalib, O Bani Abd Al-Muttalib, I cannot help you before Allah. Ask me for whatever you want of my wealth.'

h392.text: The people asked the Prophet about fortune-tellers, and he said: 'They are nothing.' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they say things that come true.' The Prophet said: 'That is a word of truth which the Jinn snatches, then he gabbles it like the clucking of a chicken into the ear of his friend, but he mixes it with more than one hundred lies.'
h392.topic: How fortune-tellers mix truth with lies

h393.text: When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His decree, like a chain beating on a rock. When the fear in their hearts subsides, they ask: 'What is it that your Lord has said?' They say: 'The truth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great.' Then those Jinn who are listening, one above another, hear this and throw it down from one to another until it reaches the fortune-teller or soothsayer. The shooting star may strike the Jinn before he passes it on, or he may pass it on first, and he adds to it one hundred lies; so it is said: 'Did he not tell us that on such and such a day such and such would happen?' So they believe him because of that one thing which was heard from the heavens.
h393.topic: How the Jinn eavesdrop and mislead soothsayers

h394.text: The angels speak in the clouds about some matter on earth, and the Shayatin overhear what they say, so they tell it to the fortune-teller, gurgling into his ear like liquid poured from a glass bottle, and he adds to it one hundred lies.

h395.text: Ka'b bin Malik said to the Prophet that Allah had revealed what He revealed about the poets. The Messenger of Allah said: 'The believer wages Jihad with his sword and with his tongue. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is as if you are attacking them with arrows.'

h396.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade the killing of four kinds of animals: ants, bees, hoopoes, and sparrow hawks.
h396.source: Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abi Dawud, Sunan Ibn Majah
h396.topic: Prohibition of killing the hoopoe and ants

isnad.name: Musnad Ahmad, Sunan Abi Dawud, Sunan Ibn Majah

h397.text: Allah, may He be exalted, says: O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, mankind and Jinn alike, were all to be as pious as the most pious among you, that would not add to My dominion in the slightest. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, mankind and Jinn alike, were all to be as evil as the most evil one among you, that would not detract from My dominion in the slightest. O My servants, these are deeds which I am recording for you, and I will judge you according to them, so whoever finds something good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.
h397.topic: Allah is Rich and self-sufficient, in need of none

h398.text: When Jibril asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) when the Hour would come, he replied: The one who is being asked about it does not know any more than the one who is asking.
h398.topic: Knowledge of the Hour belongs to Allah alone

h399.text: The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west; the smoke; the emergence of the beast; the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj; the appearance of 'Isa son of Maryam (peace be upon him); the Dajjal; and three land cave-ins, one in the west, one in the east, and one in the Arabian Peninsula; and a fire which will emerge from the midst of Yemen and will drive or gather the people, stopping with them wherever they stop for the night or to rest during the day.
h399.topic: The ten major signs before the Hour, including the beast

h400.text: The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from the west, and the emergence of the beast to mankind in the forenoon. Whichever of them appears first, the other will follow close behind it.
h400.topic: The emergence of the beast among the first signs

h401.text: Hasten to do good deeds before six things appear: the rising of the sun from the west; the smoke; the Dajjal; the beast; and the death of one of you, or general affliction.
h401.topic: Hastening to good deeds before the beast and other signs

h402.text: The Dajjal will emerge in my Ummah and will remain for forty (days, months, or years). Then Allah will send 'Isa son of Maryam, who looks like 'Urwah bin Mas'ud, and he will search for him and destroy him. Then mankind will remain for seven years during which there will not be any enmity between any two people. Then Allah will send a cool wind from the direction of Syria, and no one will be left on the face of the earth who has even a speck of goodness or faith in his heart but it will take him. Then the most evil of people will remain, and the Trumpet will be blown; no one will hear it but he will tilt his head to listen. The first to hear it will be a man setting up the tank for watering his camels, and he will fall down dead, and all the people will fall down. Then Allah will send down rain from which the bodies of the people will grow, then the Trumpet will be blown again and they will stand up looking around.
h402.topic: The blowing of the Trumpet and the resurrection

h403.text: On the day of the conquest of Makkah the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, this city was made sacred by Allah the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Resurrection. Its thorny bushes are not to be cut, its game is not to be chased, its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who will announce it publicly, and its fresh grass is not to be uprooted.
h403.topic: The sanctity of Makkah, the Lord of this city

h404.text: Musa, peace be upon him, hired himself out for the purpose of keeping chaste and to feed himself.
h404.topic: Musa hiring himself out to stay chaste and fed

h407.text: Whoever among the people of the two Books becomes Muslim, he will have his reward twice, and he has the same rights and duties as we do. Whoever among the idolators becomes Muslim will have one reward, and he has the same rights and duties as we do.
h407.topic: Double reward for the People of the Book who accept Islam

h408.text: When Abu Talib was dying, the Messenger of Allah came to him while Abu Jahl and 'Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah were with him, and said: O my uncle, say La ilaha illallah, a word which I may use as evidence in your favor before Allah. They kept urging him to remain on the religion of 'Abdul-Muttalib, and he refused to say it. The Prophet said: By Allah, I shall certainly seek forgiveness for you unless I am told not to.
h408.topic: The Prophet calling Abu Talib to faith at his death

h410.text: While a man was dragging his lower garment, he was swallowed up and he will remain sinking down into the earth until the Day of Resurrection.
h410.topic: Punishment for arrogantly dragging one's garment

h411.text: When a man among the people who came before you went out wearing two green garments, walking proudly and arrogantly, Allah commanded the earth to swallow him up, and he will remain sinking down into it until the Day of Resurrection.
h411.topic: The arrogant man swallowed by the earth

h414.text: Whoever calls others to true guidance will have a reward like that of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without it detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever calls others to misguidance will have a burden of sin like that of those who follow him until the Day of Resurrection, without it detracting from their burden in the slightest.
h414.topic: Reward for guiding others and burden for misguiding them

h415.text: Beware of injustice, for Allah will swear an oath on the Day of Resurrection and say: By My glory and majesty, no injustice will be overlooked today. Then a man will be brought forth, followed by good deeds like mountains, until he stands before the Most Merciful. The wronged will be called to come forward, and Allah will say: Settle the matter for My servant by taking from his good deeds. They will keep taking until none of his good deeds remain while people still have claims against him, so Allah will say: Take from their evil deeds and place them upon him.
h415.topic: The settling of wrongs on the Day of Resurrection

h416.text: A man came to the Prophet and said that so-and-so prays at night but steals when morning comes. The Prophet said: What you are saying (i.e., his prayer) will stop him from doing that.
h416.topic: Prayer restrains from immorality and evil

h417.text: The People of the Book used to read the Tawrah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the Muslims. The Messenger of Allah said: Do not believe the People of the Book and do not deny them. Say: We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what has been revealed to you. Our God and your God is One, and to Him we have submitted.
h417.topic: How to respond to the People of the Book

h418.text: There is no Prophet who was not given some miracles that would make the people believe in him. What I have been given is revelation which Allah revealed to me, and I hope that I will have the greatest number of followers on the Day of Resurrection.
h418.topic: The Qur'an as the Prophet's greatest miracle

h419.text: Allah says: I am testing you and testing others through you, and revealing to you a Book which cannot be washed away by water, which you recite while you are asleep and while you are awake.
h419.topic: The Qur'an preserved in the hearts

h420.text: In Paradise there are rooms whose outside can be seen from the inside and whose inside can be seen from the outside; Allah has prepared them for those who feed others, who speak good words, who pray and fast continually, and who stand in prayer at night while people are asleep.
h420.topic: The lofty dwellings of Paradise and the deeds that earn them

h421.text: When the defeat of the Romans was mentioned to the Prophet, he said, "They will certainly prevail." Abu Bakr informed the idolaters, who challenged him to set a time limit and place a wager. The Romans were later victorious as foretold.

h422.text: The Prophet said, "Allah created Adam from a handful which He took from all of the earth. So the children of Adam come in accordance with the earth; some of them come white, some red, some black, and some in between, and some evil and some good, and some easy-going and some difficult, and some in between."
h422.topic: Creation of Adam from the earth

h423.text: Allah says: "The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so; and he reviled Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying that I will not remake him as I originated him, while originating the creation is not easier for Me than re-creating him. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying that Allah has taken a son, while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient Master; I beget not, nor was I begotten, and there is none comparable to Me."
h423.topic: Repeating the creation is easy for Allah

h424.text: The Prophet said, "No child is born except in a state of Fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew or a Christian or a Zoroastrian, just as each animal produces a perfect animal like itself; do you see any among them that are born mutilated?"
h424.topic: Every child is born upon the Fitrah

h425.text: The Prophet said, "No Muslim man defends the honor of his brother except that there would be a right upon Allah to defend him from the fire of Hell on the Day of Resurrection."

h427.text: The Messenger of Allah led the people in the Fajr prayer and recited Surah Ar-Rum, but he became confused in his recitation. He said, "Our recitation of the Qur'an has been made confused for us, because some people among you are praying with us but have not performed Wudu' properly. Whoever attends the prayer with us, let him perform Wudu' properly."

h428.text: When the verse 'It is those who believe and confuse not their belief with Zulm' was revealed, the Companions were distressed and asked, 'Who among us does not wrong himself?' The Prophet said: 'That is not what it means. Have you not heard what Luqman said: O my son! Join not in worship others with Allah; verily, joining others in worship with Allah is a great wrong indeed?'

h429.text: The Messenger of Allah said that Luqman the Wise used to say: when something is entrusted to the care of Allah, He protects it.
h429.topic: Allah protects what is entrusted to Him

h430.text: The Prophet said: 'O Abu Dharr! Do you know where this sun goes?' I said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It goes and prostrates beneath the Throne, then it seeks permission from its Lord, and soon it will be said to it: Go back from whence you came.'
h430.topic: The sun runs its appointed course

h431.text: The Messenger of Allah said: There are five things which no one knows except Allah: Verily, Allah, with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, and knows that which is in the wombs; no person knows what he will earn tomorrow, and no person knows in what land he will die. Verily, Allah is All-Knower, All-Aware.
h431.topic: The five Keys of the Unseen

h432.text: The Prophet said: The Keys of the Unseen are five, which no one knows except Allah. Then he recited: Verily, Allah, with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, He sends down the rain, and knows that which is in the wombs; no person knows what he will earn tomorrow, and no person knows in what land he will die. Verily, Allah is All-Knower, All-Aware.
h432.topic: The five Keys of the Unseen

h433.text: A man came to the Prophet and asked about faith. He said: Iman is to believe in Allah, His Angels, His Books, His Messengers and in the meeting with Him, and to believe in the Resurrection. He asked about Islam. He said: Islam is to worship Allah Alone and associate nothing with Him, to establish the prayer, to pay the obligatory Zakah, and to fast in Ramadan. He asked about Ihsan. He said: Ihsan is to worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. He asked when the Hour would come. He said: The one asked about it knows no more than the one asking, but I will tell you of its signs: when the servant woman gives birth to her mistress, and when the barefoot and naked become leaders of the people. The timing of the Hour is one of the five things which no one knows except Allah. Then the man left, and the Prophet said: That was Jibril who came to teach the people their religion.
h433.topic: Iman, Islam, Ihsan and the signs of the Hour

h434.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Allah does not will that a person should die in a certain land except that He gives him a reason to go there.
h434.topic: One dies in the land decreed for him

h435.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on Fridays Alif Lam Mim As-Sajdah (Surah 32) and Hal Ata 'ala al-Insan (Surah 76).

h436.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) would not sleep until he had recited Alif Lam Mim As-Sajdah (Surah 32) and Tabarak alladhi biyadihi al-mulk (Surah 67).

h437.text: When Mu'adh asked about a deed that would admit him to Paradise and keep him from Hell, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said it is to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, establish the prayer, pay the Zakah, fast Ramadan and perform the pilgrimage. He then said: Shall I not tell you of the gates of goodness? Fasting is a shield, charity wipes out sin, and the prayer of a man in the depth of the night. He recited 'Their sides forsake their beds.' He said the head of the matter is Islam, its pillar is the prayer, and its peak is Jihad in the way of Allah, and that the whole of it depends on restraining the tongue, for people are cast into Hell on their faces only because of what their tongues reap.

h438.text: Allah says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has never crossed the mind of any human being.

h439.text: Whoever enters Paradise will enjoy a life of luxury and never feel deprivation; his clothes will never wear out and his youth will never fade. In Paradise there is what no eye has ever seen, no ear has ever heard, and what has never crossed the mind of any human being.

h441.text: There is no believer except that I am the closest of all people to him in this world and in the Hereafter. Recite if you wish: (The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves.) If any believer leaves behind wealth, let his own relatives inherit it, but if he leaves behind debt or dependents, bring them to me and I will take care of them.
h441.topic: The Prophet is closer to the believers than themselves

h442.text: O Allah, Revealer of the Book, swift in bringing to account, defeat the Confederates. O Allah, defeat them and shake them.
h442.topic: The Prophet's supplication against the Confederates

h443.text: When Allah commanded the Prophet to give his wives the choice, he came to Aisha first and said: I am going to tell you about something, and you do not have to hasten to respond until you consult your parents. Then he recited the two verses. She said: I choose Allah and His Messenger and the Home of the Hereafter.
h443.topic: Giving the wives of the Prophet the choice

h444.text: The Prophet stood to address us by the well of Khumm, and after praising Allah he said: O people, I am only a human being and soon the messenger of my Lord will come and I will answer him. I am leaving among you two weighty things: the first is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light, so hold fast to it; and the members of my household. I remind you of Allah regarding the members of my household.
h444.topic: The Book of Allah and the household of the Prophet

h445.text: Umm Salamah said: I asked the Prophet why women were not mentioned in the Qur'an as men are. Then one day he called out from the Minbar, saying: O people, Allah says: (Verily, the Muslims, men and women, the believers, men and women...) to the end of the verse.
h445.topic: Men and women mentioned together in the Qur'an

h446.text: My parable among the Prophets is that of a man who built a house and completed it well, except for the space of one brick. People would walk around it admiring it and saying: If only that brick were put in its place. Among the Prophets, I am that brick.
h446.topic: Muhammad is the last of the Prophets

h447.text: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah and offered herself to him in marriage. A man stood and asked to marry her instead. The Prophet asked what he could give as a dowry; he had nothing, not even an iron ring. The Prophet asked what he knew of the Qur'an, and the man named some Surahs. So the Prophet said: I marry her to you for what you know of the Qur'an.

h448.text: When the Prophet married Zaynab bint Jahsh, he invited the people and they ate, then some of them stayed behind talking in the house. He got up and went round to the apartments of his wives, then returned and found them still there. When they finally left and he was at the threshold, he let down the curtain between himself and me, and the verse of Hijab was revealed.
h448.topic: Revelation of the verse of Hijab

h449.text: It was said: O Messenger of Allah, we know how to send Salam upon you, but how do we send Salah upon you? He said: Say: O Allah, send Your Salah upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your Salah upon the family of Ibrahim; verily You are the Most Praiseworthy, Most Glorious. O Allah, send Your blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your blessings upon the family of Ibrahim; verily You are the Most Praiseworthy, Most Glorious.
h449.topic: How to send Salah upon the Prophet

h450.text: Allah says: The son of Adam annoys Me by inveighing against time, but I am time; I cause the alternation of night and day.

h451.text: The Messenger of Allah heard Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari reciting Qur'an at night, and he stopped and listened, then said: This man has been given one of the sweet, melodious voices of the Prophet Dawud.

h452.text: The most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud: he used to sleep half the night, stand in prayer for a third of it, and sleep for a sixth of it. The most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud: he used to fast one day and not fast the next, and he never fled from the battlefield.
h452.topic: The prayer and fast of Dawud

h453.text: A man asked the Messenger of Allah about Saba' - whether it was a land or a woman. He said: It was neither a land nor a woman; it was a man who had ten children, six of whom went to Yemen and four of whom went to Ash-Sham. Those who went to Ash-Sham were Lakhm, Judham, Amilah and Ghassan; those who went south were Kindah, al-Ash'ariyyun, al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar and Anmar.

h454.text: How amazing is the affair of the believer! Allah does not decree anything for him but it is good for him. If something good happens to him, he gives thanks, and that is good for him; and if something bad happens to him, he bears it with patience, and that is good for him. This is not the case for anyone except the believer.
h454.topic: Patience and gratitude of the believer

h455.text: When Allah decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His words, making a sound like a chain striking a smooth rock. When the fear is banished from their hearts, they say, What is it that your Lord has said? They say the truth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. Then the eavesdropping devil hears it and passes it down from one to another until it reaches the lips of a soothsayer, who mixes it with a hundred lies.
h455.topic: The angels and the decree of Allah

h456.text: I have been given five things which were not given to any Prophet before me: I have been aided by fear cast into the enemy at a distance of a month's journey; the whole earth has been made a place of prayer and a means of purification for me, so whoever of my Ummah is overtaken by the time of prayer may pray; the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given the power of intercession; and whereas every Prophet before me was sent only to his own people, I have been sent to all of mankind.
h456.topic: The Prophet sent to all mankind

h457.text: Allah does not look at your outward appearance or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
h457.topic: Allah looks at the heart, not wealth

h459.text: When the Messenger of Allah entered the Sacred Mosque on the day of the conquest of Makkah and found the idols standing around the Ka'bah, he began striking them with his bow while reciting: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; surely falsehood is ever bound to vanish; and: The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor restore it.
h459.topic: Destroying the idols at the conquest of Makkah

h460.text: You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent; you are calling upon One Who is All-Hearing, Ever Near and Responsive.
h460.topic: Allah is All-Hearing and Ever Near

h461.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to say when he finished praying: There is no god worthy of worship except Allah alone, with no partner. To Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs all praise, and He is able to do all things. O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You give, and none who can give what You withhold, and no good fortune or wealth can benefit anyone against Your will.
h461.topic: Supplication after prayer; none can withhold what Allah gives

h462.text: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) raised his head from bowing, he would say: Allah hears those who praise Him. O Allah, our Lord, to You be praise filling the heavens and the earth and filling whatever You wish besides. O Allah, the One deserving praise and glory; the truest words a servant says, and all of us are Your servants: O Allah, there is none who can withhold what You give, and none who can give what You withhold, and no wealth or majesty can benefit anyone against Your will.

h463.text: Those who remember Allah and glorify Him by saying 'Glory be to Allah, Allah is Most Great, all praise is due to Allah, and there is no god but Allah' — these words go around the Throne, buzzing like bees, mentioning the one who said them. Would one of you not like to have something with Allah that mentions him?
h463.topic: Words of remembrance ascend to the Throne

h465.text: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: Whoever would like to have ample provision and a long life, let him uphold the ties of kinship.
h465.topic: Upholding ties of kinship extends provision and life

h466.text: Whoever follows a path seeking knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise. The angels lower their wings out of pleasure for the seeker of knowledge. Whoever is in the heavens and the earth, even the fish in the water, seek forgiveness for the scholar. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like that of the moon over all the other heavenly bodies. The scholars are the heirs of the Prophets, for the Prophets leave behind neither dinar nor dirham; they leave behind only knowledge, and whoever takes it has taken an abundant share.
h466.source: Musnad Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah
h466.source_short: Ahmad, Abu Dawud, Tirmidhi & Ibn Majah
h466.topic: Virtue of seeking knowledge; scholars are heirs of the Prophets

isnad.name: Musnad Ahmad, Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah

h467.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said one day: My intercession will be for those among my Ummah who commit major sins.
h467.topic: The Prophet's intercession for those who commit major sins

h468.text: The ornaments of the believer will reach as far as his ablution reaches.
h468.topic: The believer's ornaments in Paradise and ablution

h469.text: Allah has left no excuse for a man whose life He prolonged until he reached the age of sixty.
h469.topic: No excuse remains for one who lives to sixty

h470.text: The usual life span in my Ummah is between sixty and seventy years, and only a few of them pass that.
h470.topic: The typical lifespan of this Ummah

h471.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to command us to make our prayers short, and he used to recite As-Saffat when he led us in prayer.

h472.text: We have been favored over the rest of mankind in three ways: our ranks have been made like the ranks of the angels; the entire earth has been made a Masjid for us; and its soil has been made a means of purification for us if we cannot find water.
h472.topic: Ranks of the believers like the ranks of the angels

h473.text: Will you not form ranks as the angels form ranks in the presence of their Lord? They asked how the angels form ranks, and he said: They complete the rows nearer the front and they consolidate the rows.
h473.topic: Straightening the prayer rows like the angels

h474.text: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say La ilaha illallah. Whoever says La ilaha illallah, he and his property are safe from me except for his obligation, and his reckoning will be with Allah.
h474.topic: The testimony of La ilaha illallah

h475.text: Concerning the words 'his progeny, them We made the survivors,' the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Sam, Ham and Yafith. Sam was the father of the Arabs, Ham was the father of the Ethiopians, and Yafith was the father of the Romans.

h476.text: Ibrahim did not lie except in three cases: two were for the sake of Allah, when he said 'Verily, I am sick,' and when he said 'Nay, this one, the biggest of them did it'; and when he said concerning his wife Sarah, 'She is my sister.'

h477.text: Allah has created every doer of deeds and what he does.
h477.topic: Allah is the creator of the servants and their deeds

h478.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: I saw the horns of the ram when I entered the House (the Ka'bah), and I forgot to tell you to cover them up; cover them up, for there should not be anything in the House which could distract the worshipper.
h478.topic: The horns of the ram sacrificed in place of Isma'il

h479.text: It is not right for any person to say I am better than Yunus bin Matta.
h479.topic: The status of the Prophet Yunus

h480.text: On the morning of Khaybar, when its people came out with their tools and saw the army, they turned back saying 'Muhammad, by Allah!' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Allahu Akbar! Khaybar has been destroyed. When it descends in the courtyard of any people, evil will be the morning for those who had been warned.

h481.text: The most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud, and the most beloved fasting to Allah is the fasting of Dawud. He used to sleep for half of the night, stand in prayer for a third of the night, then sleep for a sixth of the night, and he used to fast on alternate days. He never fled from the battlefield, and he always turned to Allah.
h481.topic: The prayer and fasting of Dawud

h482.text: Ibn 'Abbas said: The prostration in Surah Sad is not one of the obligatory prostrations, yet I saw the Messenger of Allah prostrating in it.

h483.text: The Prophet prostrated in Surah Sad and said: Dawud prostrated as an act of repentance, and we prostrate as an act of thanks.
h483.topic: Reason for the prostration in Surah Sad

h484.text: The Messenger of Allah recited Surah Sad while on the Minbar. When he reached the place of prostration he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated with him. On another occasion when he recited it and reached the prostration, the people prepared to prostrate, so he said: This is repentance for a Prophet, but I see that you are preparing to prostrate. Then he came down and prostrated.
h484.topic: The Prophet's prostration when reciting Surah Sad

h485.text: The Messenger of Allah returned from a campaign, and a wind lifted a curtain in 'A'ishah's room, revealing her toys, among them a horse with two wings of cloth. He asked, What is this that I see among them? She said, A horse. He said, And what is this on it? She said, Wings. He said, A horse with two wings? She said, Did you not hear that Sulayman had a horse that had wings? Then the Messenger of Allah smiled so broadly that his molars could be seen.

h486.text: On the day of the Trench, 'Umar came after the sun had set and said, O Messenger of Allah, I could hardly pray 'Asr until the sun had almost set. The Messenger of Allah said, By Allah, I did not pray it either. So we went to Buthan, and the Prophet performed ablution and we performed ablution, and he prayed 'Asr after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.
h486.topic: Missing 'Asr prayer on the day of the Trench

h487.text: An 'Ifrit from among the Jinn came and bothered me last night, trying to stop me from praying. Allah enabled me to overpower him, and I wanted to tie him to one of the pillars of the Masjid so that you could see him this morning. Then I remembered the words of my brother Sulayman: My Lord, forgive me and bestow upon me a kingdom such as shall not belong to any other after me. So I let him go, humiliated.
h487.topic: Sulayman's unique kingdom and the captured Jinn

h488.text: The Messenger of Allah stood to pray and we heard him say, I seek refuge with Allah from you, then, I curse you with the complete curse of Allah, three times, while stretching out his hand as if to seize something. Afterward he explained: The enemy of Allah, Iblis, came with a flame of fire to throw in my face, so I sought refuge with Allah from him three times and cursed him with the complete curse of Allah, but he did not retreat. Then I wanted to seize him, and by Allah, were it not for the words of our brother Sulayman, he would have been chained up and become a plaything for the children of the people of Al-Madinah.
h488.topic: Sulayman's prayer and seeking refuge from Iblis

h489.text: While Ayyub was bathing naked, locusts of gold fell upon him, and he began gathering them in his garment. Then his Lord called to him: O Ayyub, have I not made you so rich that you have no need of what you see? He said: Yes, O Lord, but I cannot do without Your blessing.
h489.topic: Ayyub and the locusts of gold

h491.text: The Messenger of Allah used to fast until we would say he did not want to break his fast, and he would not fast until we would say he did not want to fast. And he used to recite Bani Isra'il (Al-Isra') and Az-Zumar every night.

h492.text: The people of Paradise will look towards each other in the raised places of Paradise as you look at the high, bright stars which remain on the horizon. Such will be the difference in superiority which some of them have over others. They asked: O Messenger of Allah, are those the abodes of the Prophets? He said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are the abodes of people who believed in Allah and in the Messengers.

h493.text: Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; be mindful of Allah and you will find Him ever with you. Turn to Allah in times of ease and He will turn to you in times of difficulty. If you ask, ask Allah; if you seek help, seek help from Allah. Know that if the whole nation were to gather to benefit you with something, they could not benefit you except with what Allah has decreed for you, and if they gathered to harm you with something, they could not harm you except with what Allah has decreed against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried. Know that in patiently bearing what you dislike there is much good, that victory comes with patience, that relief comes with distress, and that with hardship comes ease.
h493.topic: Reliance on Allah and divine decree

h494.text: When anyone of you goes to bed, let him dust off his bed with the inside of his lower garment, for he does not know what came onto it after he left it. Then let him say: In Your Name, my Lord, I lay down my side, and in Your Name I raise it up. If You take my soul, have mercy on it, and if You send it back, protect it with that by which You protect Your righteous servants.

h495.text: When the Messenger of Allah stood up to pray at night, he would begin his prayer with the words: O Allah, Lord of Jibril, Mika'il and Israfil, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, You will judge between Your servants concerning that wherein they differ. Guide me, by Your leave, to the truth concerning that wherein there is dispute, for You guide whomsoever You will to a straight path.
h495.topic: Opening supplication for the night prayer

h496.text: If you did not commit sins, Allah would create people who would commit sins so that He could forgive them.

h497.text: Each of the people of Hell will be shown his place in Paradise and will say: If only Allah had guided me; so it will be a source of regret for him. And each of the people of Paradise will be shown his place in Hell and will say: Had Allah not guided me; so it will be a cause of thankfulness for him.
h497.topic: Regret and gratitude in the Hereafter

h498.text: A rabbi came to the Messenger of Allah and said: O Muhammad, we find that Allah will place the heavens on one finger, the earths on one finger, the trees on one finger, the water and dust on one finger, and the rest of creation on one finger, then He will say: I am the King. The Messenger of Allah smiled so broadly that his molars could be seen, in confirmation of what the rabbi said, then he recited: They did not make a just estimate of Allah such as is due to Him, and on the Day of Resurrection the whole earth will be grasped by His Hand.
h498.topic: The greatness of Allah on the Day of Resurrection

h499.text: Between the two blasts of the Trumpet there will be forty. They asked: O Abu Hurairah, forty days? He said: I decline to answer. They asked: Forty years? He said: I decline to answer. They asked: Forty months? He said: I decline to answer. Then he said: Every part of a man will decay except the root of his tailbone, and from it the creation will be reassembled.
h499.topic: The interval between the two blasts of the Trumpet

h500.text: Seventy thousand of my Ummah will enter Paradise with their faces shining like the moon on the night when it is full. Ukkashah bin Mihsan stood up and said: O Messenger of Allah, pray to Allah to make me one of them. He said: O Allah, make him one of them. Then a man from the Ansar stood up and said the same, and he said: Ukkashah has beaten you to it.
h500.topic: Those who enter Paradise without reckoning

h501.text: When a Muslim supplicates for his brother in his absence, the angel says: 'Amin, and may you have the like.'
h501.topic: Angels say Amin to prayers made in a brother's absence

h502.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say after every prescribed prayer: 'There is no true god except Allah alone, with no partner; His is the dominion and praise, and He is able to do all things. There is no strength and no power except with Allah. There is no true god except Allah, and we worship none but Him; His are the blessing, the bounty and the goodly praise. There is no true god except Allah, we worship Him in all sincerity even though the disbelievers hate it.'
h502.topic: The Prophet's words of remembrance after every prayer

h503.text: Allah, the Exalted, said: 'O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another... O My servants, these are your deeds which I record for you, then I will recompense you for them. So whoever finds good, let him praise Allah, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.'
h503.topic: Allah forbids injustice and recompenses servants by their deeds

h504.text: While the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was praying in the courtyard of the Ka'bah, 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'it came, seized his shoulder and twisted his garment around his neck, strangling him severely. Abu Bakr came, took 'Uqbah by the shoulder and pushed him away from the Prophet, then said: 'Would you kill a man because he says: My Lord is Allah, and he has come to you with clear signs from your Lord?'
h504.topic: Abu Bakr defends the Prophet from 'Uqbah bin Abi Mu'it

h505.text: When one of you dies, his place is shown to him morning and evening: if he is one of the people of Paradise, then from the people of Paradise, and if he is one of the people of the Fire, then from the people of the Fire. It is said to him: This is your place until Allah resurrects you to it on the Day of Resurrection.
h505.topic: The dead are shown their place morning and evening

h506.text: A'ishah asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) whether there would be torment in the grave before the Day of Resurrection, after a Jewish woman mentioned it. Later he came out at midday, his eyes reddened, calling aloud: 'The grave is like patches of dark night! O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge with Allah from the torment of the grave, for the torment of the grave is real.'
h506.grade: Its chain is Sahih according to the conditions of Al-Bukhari and Muslim
h506.topic: The Prophet affirms the reality of the torment of the grave

h507.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Verily, you will be tested in the graves.' After that he used to seek refuge with Allah from the torment of the grave.
h507.topic: People will be tested in their graves

h508.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, supplication is worship,' and then recited: 'And your Lord said: Call upon Me, I will answer you.'
h508.topic: Supplication is the essence of worship

h509.text: The Prophet laughed and said he was amazed at how a servant will dispute with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. The servant will say, 'My Lord, did You not promise me that You would not treat me unjustly?' Allah will say, 'Yes.' The man will say, 'I will not accept any witness against me except from myself.' Allah will say, 'Is it not sufficient that I and the angels, the noble scribes, are witnesses?' This will be repeated several times, then a seal will be placed over his mouth and his limbs will speak about what he used to do. Then he will say, 'Away with you! It was only for your sake that I was arguing.'
h509.topic: A servant disputing with his Lord and his limbs testifying

h510.text: Sufyan ibn Abdullah Ath-Thaqafi said, 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me something that I can adhere to.' He said: 'Say, my Lord is Allah, then stand firm.' I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?' The Messenger of Allah took hold of the edge of his tongue and said, 'This.'
h510.topic: Saying 'My Lord is Allah' and standing firm; guarding the tongue

h512.text: The Mu'adhdhins will be the ones with the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection.

h513.text: The Imam is a guarantor and the Mu'adhdhin is in a position of trust. May Allah guide the Imams and forgive the Mu'adhdhins.
h513.topic: The responsibility of the Imam and the Mu'adhdhin

h515.text: Al-Harith bin Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah how revelation came to him. He said: "Sometimes it comes to me like the ringing of a bell, which is the most difficult for me; then it goes away and I understand what was said. And sometimes the angel comes to me in the image of a man, and he speaks to me and I understand what he says." Aishah said she saw him receiving revelation on a very cold day, and when it departed from him there were beads of sweat on his forehead.
h515.topic: How revelation came to the Prophet

h516.narrator: Abdullah bin Adi bin Al-Hamra Az-Zuhri (RA)
h516.text: The Messenger of Allah said, while standing in the marketplace of Makkah: "By Allah, you are the best land of Allah, the most beloved land to Allah; were it not for the fact that I was driven out from you, I would never have left you."
h516.topic: Makkah, the Mother of the Towns

isnad.name: Abdullah bin Adi bin Al-Hamra Az-Zuhri (RA)

h517.text: The Messenger of Allah came out holding two books. Concerning the one in his right hand he said: "This is a book from the Lord of the worlds, containing the names of the people of Paradise and of their fathers and tribes; all of them are detailed down to the last one, and nothing will be added or taken away from it." Concerning the one in his left hand he said: "This is the book of the people of Hell, containing their names and the names of their fathers and tribes, all detailed down to the last one, and nothing will be added or taken away from it." When asked why they should strive if the matter is already settled, he said: "Strive with your deeds as hard as you can for the middle course or close to it, for the person destined for Paradise will die doing the deeds of the people of Paradise, and the person destined for Hell will die doing the deeds of the people of Hell."
h517.topic: Decree of the people of Paradise and Hell

h519.text: The Messenger of Allah said: "Allah is more pleased with the repentance of His servant than any one of you who loses his riding beast in a barren land, while it carries his food and drink; he despairs of finding it, so he comes to a tree and lies down in its shade, having given up hope; then suddenly he sees it standing near him, so he takes hold of its reins, and out of his great joy he says by mistake, 'O Allah, You are my slave and I am Your Lord!'"
h519.topic: Allah's joy at the repentance of His servant

h520.text: The Messenger of Allah said: "No physical harm befalls a believer, but Allah will expiate some of his sins because of it."

h521.text: The Messenger of Allah said: "If a person commits many sins and has nothing that will expiate for them, Allah will test him with some grief that will expiate for them."

h523.text: If this world were worth a gnat's wing before Allah, He would never give a disbeliever a drink of water.
h523.topic: The insignificance of this world before Allah

h524.text: Do not drink from vessels of gold and silver, and do not eat from plates of the same, for these things are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter.
h524.topic: Prohibition of gold and silver vessels

h526.text: When you see that Allah gives a person what he wants even though he is persisting in sin, that means that Allah is enticing him into destruction.
h526.topic: Worldly favor amid persistent sin as a gradual ensnarement

h527.text: No people go astray after having been guided, but they resort to futile argument.
h527.topic: Quarrelsome argument as a cause of misguidance

h528.text: Ya'la bin Umayyah said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) reciting on the Minbar: And they will cry: O Malik! Let your Lord make an end of us.
h528.topic: The people of Hell pleading for death

h529.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to Ibn Sayyad, 'I am concealing something for you,' while he was concealing from him the words 'Then wait you for the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke.' Ibn Sayyad said, 'It is Ad-Dukh.' The Prophet said, 'Be off with you! You cannot get further than your rank.'

h530.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) looked out upon us while we were discussing the Hour and said, 'The Hour will not come until you see ten signs: the rising of the sun from the west, the smoke, the beast, the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, the appearance of 'Isa son of Maryam, the Dajjal, three cases of the earth collapsing (one in the east, one in the west, and one in the Arabian Peninsula), and a fire which will emerge from the bottom of Aden and drive the people, staying with them where they stop at night and where they rest during the day.'
h530.topic: The ten signs of the Hour

h532.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Death will be brought forth in the image of a fine ram. It will be made to stand between Paradise and Hell, then it will be slaughtered. It will be said, "O people of Paradise, it is eternal, no more death; and O people of Hell, it is eternal, no more death."'
h532.topic: Death slaughtered, eternity in the Hereafter

h533.narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) and Abu Hurairah (RA)
h533.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'It will be said to the people of Paradise: It is granted to you that you will be healthy and never fall ill, you will live and never die, you will enjoy a life of luxury and never be miserable, and you will be youthful and never grow old.'
h533.topic: Everlasting bliss of the people of Paradise

isnad.name: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) and Abu Hurairah (RA)

h534.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Work and strive hard, and know that no one will enter Paradise by virtue of his deeds.' They said, 'Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'Not even me, unless Allah showers me with His mercy and grace.'

h535.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) prohibited traveling with the Qur'an to the lands of the enemy, for fear that the Qur'an might be desecrated by the enemy.
h535.topic: Not taking the Qur'an into enemy territory

h536.text: Allah the Exalted says: The son of Adam annoys Me when he curses Ad-Dahr (time), while I am Ad-Dahr. In My Hand are all matters; I cause the alternation of his days and nights. In another wording: Do not curse Ad-Dahr (time), for Allah is Ad-Dahr.

h539.text: Allah the Exalted said: Glory is My robe and pride is My garment; whoever rivals Me for either of them, I will make him reside in My Fire.

h540.text: Umm Al-Ala' said that when Uthman bin Maz'un died in her house she declared that Allah had honored him. The Prophet (peace be upon him) asked, "How do you know that Allah has honored him?" She said she did not know. He said, "As for him, certainty (death) has reached him from his Lord, and I surely wish well for him. But by Allah, even though I am Allah's Messenger, I do not know what will happen to me."
h540.topic: Not declaring a specific person's fate

h541.text: I have not heard Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) say about anyone walking on the surface of the earth that he is of the people of Paradise, except for Abdullah bin Salam.
h541.topic: Abdullah bin Salam among the people of Paradise

h543.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: May Allah have mercy on us and on the Brother of 'Ad.

h544.text: Aishah said that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would never laugh fully but only smile, and that when he saw clouds or wind, discomfort would appear on his face. She asked why, when people rejoice at clouds hoping for rain, displeasure showed on his face. He replied: O Aishah, what assures me that they do not bring punishment? A nation was punished with wind, and on seeing the punishment approaching they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."
h544.topic: The Prophet's caution at wind and clouds

h545.text: Aishah said that when the wind blew, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would say: O Allah, I ask You of its good, the good that it contains, and the good with which it has been sent; and I seek refuge in You from its evil, the evil that it contains, and the evil with which it has been sent.

h546.text: Aishah said that when the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saw clouds on the horizon he would leave whatever he was doing, even in prayer, and say: O Allah, I seek refuge with You from any harm it contains. If Allah removed the clouds he would praise Him, and if rain fell he would say: O Allah, make it a beneficial downpour.
h546.topic: Supplication on seeing clouds and rain

h547.text: After the believers safely pass the Fire on the Day of Judgement, they will be detained on a bridge between Paradise and the Fire, where any wrongs they committed against one another in the world will be settled. Once they are purified and cleansed, they will be admitted into Paradise; and by the One in whose Hand is my soul, each of them will find his way to his dwelling in Paradise better than he knew his way to his dwelling in the world.
h547.topic: Believers guided to their homes in Paradise

h548.text: In Paradise there is a lake of milk, a lake of water, a lake of honey, and a lake of wine, and the rivers then gush forth from them.

h549.text: I have been sent before the Hour like these two, holding up his index and middle fingers together.

h550.text: When Allah finished creating the creation, the womb stood up and took hold of the lower garment of the Most Merciful. He said, Stop that. It said, This is the place of one seeking refuge in You from being severed. Allah said, Would it not please you that I join whoever joins you and sever whoever severs you? It said, Yes indeed. He said, That is granted to you.

h551.text: The womb is attached to the Throne. The one who keeps good relations is not the one who reciprocates; rather, the one who truly keeps the ties is he who restores them when his kinfolk have severed them.

h552.text: No sin is more deserving that Allah hasten its punishment in this world, along with what He stores up for its doer in the Hereafter, than injustice and severing the ties of kinship.

h553.text: As the first drop of his blood gushes forth, a martyr is granted six things: all his sins are forgiven, he is shown his place in Paradise, he is married to wide-eyed maidens, he is secured from the greatest terror and from the torment of the grave, and he is clothed with the adornment of faith.

h554.text: A martyr is allowed to intercede for seventy members of his household.

h555.text: Allah's Messenger recited Surah Al-Fath on the day of the conquest of Makkah while riding his she-camel, reciting it in a vibrating and pleasant tone.
