h556.text: The Prophet said: Last night a Surah was revealed to me that is dearer to me than this life and all that it contains, then he recited: Verily, We have given you a manifest victory, that Allah may forgive you your sins of the past and the future.
h556.topic: The surah dearer than the world

h557.text: The Prophet used to pray until both his feet were swollen. He was asked, Has not Allah forgiven you all your past and future sins? He said: Should I not be a thankful servant?

h558.text: The Prophet said, while he was with Hafsah: Allah willing, none of the Companions of the tree, who gave the pledge under it, will ever enter Hellfire.
h558.topic: Those who pledged under the tree

h559.text: When a slave of Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah complained that Hatib would surely enter Hell, the Messenger of Allah replied: You lie, he shall never enter the Fire, for he participated in Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah.
h559.topic: Virtue of the people of Hudaybiyyah

h560.text: The Prophet said: None among those who gave the pledge under the tree shall enter Hellfire.
h560.topic: Reward of the pledge of Ar-Ridwan

h561.text: The Messenger of Allah said: O Allah, be merciful to those who have their heads shaved. The people said, And those who get their hair cut short? He repeated, O Allah, be merciful to those who have their heads shaved, and only after the third or fourth time added: And to those who get their hair cut short.
h561.topic: Supplication for those who shaved their heads

h564.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Do not abuse my Companions, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach the level of a Mudd given by one of them, nor half of it.

h565.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) missed Thabit bin Qays, and a man went to find him and found him sitting at home with his head lowered. Thabit said he feared his deeds were ruined because he had raised his voice above the voice of the Prophet, and that he was among the people of the Fire. When this was conveyed to the Prophet (peace be upon him), he said, 'Go back to him and tell him: you are not among the people of the Fire. Rather, you are among the dwellers of Paradise.'
h565.topic: Thabit bin Qays and lowering the voice before the Prophet

h566.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) gave a speech upon the pulpit while Al-Hasan bin Ali was with him, looking now at Al-Hasan and now at the people, and said, 'Verily, this son of mine is a chief, and may Allah make peace between two great groups of Muslims through him.'
h566.topic: Reconciliation between two groups of Muslims

h567.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Help your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed.' It was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, I help him if he is oppressed, but how do I help him if he is an oppressor?' He said, 'By preventing him from oppressing others; this is how you help him.'
h567.topic: Helping the oppressor and the oppressed

h568.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'Beware of suspicion, for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy on one another, do not seek out one another's faults, do not envy one another, do not hate one another, and do not turn away from one another. And be, O servants of Allah, brothers.'
h568.topic: Prohibition of suspicion, spying, and backbiting

h569.text: Some people asked the Prophet (peace be upon him), 'Who is the most honorable of people?' He said, 'The most honorable of them before Allah is the one with the most Taqwa.' They said, 'We did not ask you about this.' He said, 'Then the most honorable person is Yusuf, Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's Prophet, the son of Allah's close friend (Ibrahim).' They said, 'We did not ask you about this.' He said, 'Then you ask me about the origins of the Arabs? The best of you in the time of ignorance are the best of you in Islam, if they attain understanding of the religion.'
h569.topic: Honor is by Taqwa, not lineage

h570.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) gave to some men and gave nothing to one of them. Sad said, 'O Messenger of Allah, you gave to so-and-so and so-and-so, but you gave nothing to so-and-so, even though he is a believer.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Or a Muslim,' and he repeated this each time Sad repeated his words. Then he said, 'I give to some men while leaving others who are dearer to me than them, giving them nothing, for fear that they be thrown on their faces into the Fire.'
h570.topic: The distinction between Iman and Islam

h571.text: Jahannam will be asked, "Are you full?" and it will say, "Are there any more?" Until the Lord, the Blessed and Most Honored, puts His Foot over it, and it will say: "Enough! Enough!"
h571.topic: Hell asks if there are any more

h572.text: Paradise and the Fire quarreled. The Fire said, "I have been favored with the arrogant people and tyrants." Paradise said, "What is wrong with me that only the poor and humble people enter me?" Allah said to Paradise, "You are My mercy, with which I grant mercy to those whom I will among My servants." He said to the Fire, "You are My punishment which I inflict upon whom I wish from My servants, and I shall fill both of you." As for the Fire, it will not have its fill until Allah puts His Foot over it and it will say, "Enough! Enough!" As for Paradise, Allah will create another creation to fill it.

h573.text: The people will be thrown into Jahannam and it will say, "Are there any more?" until the Mighty Lord puts His Foot over it and its corners will be drawn together, and it will say, "Enough, enough, by Your grace and compassion!" There will remain empty space in Paradise until Allah creates another creation whom He will make dwell in the empty parts of Paradise.
h573.topic: Hell filled and Paradise's remaining space

h574.text: Certainly you will be brought before your Lord and will see Him as you see this moon, and you will have no trouble in seeing Him. So if you can avoid missing the prayer before the rising of the sun and the prayer before its setting, then do so.
h574.topic: Seeing the Lord and guarding the two prayers

h575.text: Shall I tell you about something that, if you did it, you would catch up with those who have surpassed you, and nobody would be better than you except those who would do the same? Say Subhan Allah, Alhamdulillah, and Allahu Akbar thirty-three times each after every prayer.

h576.text: The earth will open up first around me.
h576.topic: The Prophet first raised on the Day of Resurrection

h578.text: Verily, there are lofty rooms in Paradise whose outside can be seen from inside and whose inside can be seen from outside. They are for those who use soft speech, feed food, and spend the night in voluntary prayer while people are asleep.
h578.topic: Reward of those who pray at night

h579.text: Allah, the Most High, descends each night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains and says: Is there anyone repenting, that I may accept his repentance? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness, that I may forgive him? Is there anyone asking of Me, that I may grant him his request? This continues until dawn begins.
h579.topic: Allah's descent and seeking forgiveness before dawn

h580.text: The poor person (Miskin) is not the one who goes around to people and is turned away with a morsel or two, or a date or two. Rather, the poor person is the one who does not have enough to satisfy his needs and whose condition is not known to others, so that charity may be given to him.
h580.topic: The truly needy who do not beg

h581.text: I have been made victorious with the Saba (the easterly wind), and the people of Ad were destroyed with the Dabur (the westerly wind).
h581.topic: The winds and the destruction of Ad

h582.text: Allah the Exalted said: O Son of Adam! Devote yourself to My worship and I will fill your chest with riches and remove your poverty. But if you do not, I will fill your chest with preoccupations and will not remove your poverty.
h582.topic: Devoting oneself to the worship of Allah

h583.text: The Messenger of Allah taught the recitation: Verily, I am the Provider, the Owner of power, the Most Strong.

h584.text: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) reciting Surat At-Tur while praying Maghrib, and I have never heard a more beautiful voice or recitation than his.
h584.topic: The Prophet reciting Surat At-Tur in Maghrib

h585.text: Umm Salamah complained to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) of being ill, and he said, 'Perform Tawaf of the Ka'bah behind the crowd while you are riding.' So she performed Tawaf while the Messenger of Allah was praying beside the House, reciting Surat At-Tur.
h585.topic: Performing Tawaf while riding when ill

h586.text: When the son of Adam dies, his record of deeds ceases except in three cases: an ongoing charity, knowledge that people benefit from, and a righteous child who supplicates for him.

h587.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Verily, the believers and their offspring will dwell in Paradise, while the idolaters and their offspring will dwell in the Hellfire,' and then he recited, 'And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith.'
h587.topic: Believers and their offspring in Paradise

h588.text: I heard the Prophet (peace be upon him) recite Surat At-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, and when he reached the verses, 'Or were they created by nothing? Or were they themselves the creators? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, but they have no firm belief. Or are with them the treasures of your Lord? Or are they the tyrants with the authority to do as they like?', I felt my heart would fly away.
h588.topic: The effect of these verses on the listener

h589.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was never more regular and particular in offering any voluntary prayer than the two Sunnah Rak'ahs of the Fajr prayer.

h590.text: Surat An-Najm was the first Surah in which a prostration was revealed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) recited it in Makkah and prostrated, and those with him prostrated too, except an old man who took a handful of soil and prostrated on it; he was later seen killed as a disbeliever.

h591.text: Write down what you hear from me. By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, nothing comes out of me except the truth.

h592.text: I saw Jibril (in his original form), and he had six hundred wings.
h592.topic: The Prophet saw Jibril in his true form

h593.text: Abu Dharr asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) whether he had seen his Lord. He replied that there was only light, and in another wording, that he saw only a light.
h593.topic: Did the Prophet see his Lord

h594.text: Aisha said she was the first of this Ummah to ask the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about this, and he said that it was Jibril; he saw him in his real form only twice, descending from heaven so huge that he filled the horizon between sky and earth.
h594.topic: What the Prophet saw was Jibril

h595.text: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey, he ascended to Sidrat al-Muntaha in the seventh heaven, and he was given three things: the five daily prayers, the concluding verses of Surat al-Baqarah, and forgiveness of grave sins for those of his Ummah who do not associate anything with Allah.
h595.topic: What was granted at Sidrat al-Muntaha

h596.text: Allah has decreed for the son of Adam his share of Zina, which he will inevitably attain: the Zina of the eye is looking, the Zina of the tongue is speech, and the soul wishes and desires, while the private part either confirms that or denies it.

h597.text: Do not ascribe purity to yourselves; Allah knows best who among you are the pious. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was told a girl was named Barrah (the pious one), he forbade the name and said she should be called Zaynab instead.
h597.topic: Do not claim purity for yourself

h598.text: When a man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet (peace be upon him), he said: Woe to you, you have cut off the neck of your companion. If one of you must praise his companion, let him say, 'I reckon so-and-so to be such, and Allah is his reckoner, and I do not purify anyone before Allah,' if he truly knows that of him.

h599.text: When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: an ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is derived, or a righteous child who supplicates for him.

h600.text: The people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah to produce a miracle, so he showed them the splitting of the moon into two parts, until they saw the mount of Hira between them.

h601.text: The moon was split into two parts during the time of the Messenger of Allah, and the people saw its two parts. The Messenger of Allah said: Be witnesses.

h602.text: I was sent like this with the Last Hour, and he pointed with his middle and index fingers.

h603.text: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recited to the Prophet 'then is there any that will remember,' and the Prophet recited it back to him correcting the pronunciation as 'fahal min muddakir.'

h604.text: On the day of the battle of Badr, while in his tent, the Prophet supplicated: O Allah, I ask You for the fulfillment of Your covenant and promise. O Allah, if You wish, You will never be worshipped on the earth after today. Abu Bakr took him by the hand and said this is enough. The Prophet, clad in his armor, then went out reciting: Their multitude will be put to flight and they will show their backs; nay, but the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour will be more grievous and more bitter.

h605.text: Everything is by decree, even incapacity and intelligence.

h606.text: Allah recorded the measurements of the creation fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth.

h607.text: The first thing Allah created was the Pen. Then He said to it: Write. So at that moment it recorded everything that will happen until the Day of Resurrection.

h608.text: O Aishah, beware of the sins that are belittled, for there is someone appointed by Allah who records them.

h609.text: The just will be with Allah on pulpits of light, at the right of the Most Merciful, and both of His Hands are right; they are those who are just in their judgement and with their families and those under their care.

h610.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited Surat Ar-Rahman from beginning to end to his Companions, but they remained silent. He said: I recited it to the Jinn on the night of the Jinn, and their response was better than yours. Whenever I reached the words 'Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny?' they would say: None of Your favors, our Lord, do we deny, so all praise is due to You.
h610.topic: The Jinn's response to the surah's refrain

h611.text: The angels were created from light, the Jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you.
h611.topic: Creation of angels, jinn, and Adam

h612.text: There are two gardens whose vessels and all that they contain are of silver, and two gardens whose vessels and all that they contain are of gold. Nothing will stand between the people and looking at their Lord, the Mighty and Honored, except the covering of pride over His Face in the Garden of Eden.
h612.topic: The two Gardens for those who fear their Lord

h613.text: The first group to enter Paradise will look like the moon on the night when it is full, and the group following them will be as radiant as the brightest shining star in the sky. Each man among them will have two wives, the marrow of whose shin-bones will be seen through the flesh. There will be no unmarried person in Paradise.
h613.topic: The wives of the people of Paradise

h614.text: A morning or an evening journey in the cause of Allah is better than the world and all that is in it. A place in Paradise as small as the space taken up by the whip of one of you is better than the world and all that is in it. And if a woman of the people of Paradise were to look down upon the earth, she would fill what is between Paradise and the earth with fragrance and make it pleasant, and the veil over her head is better than this world and all that is in it.

h615.text: In Paradise the believer will have a tent made of a single hollow pearl, sixty miles wide. In it the believer will have wives whom he visits, and they do not see one another.

h616.text: When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) finished the prayer with the Salam, he would remain seated only long enough to say: O Allah, You are As-Salam, and from You comes peace; blessed are You, O Owner of Majesty and Honor.
h616.topic: Remembrance of the Owner of Majesty and Honor after prayer

h617.text: Persist in invoking Allah with: O Owner of Majesty and Honor.
h617.topic: Invoking Allah by His attribute of Majesty and Honor

h618.text: Abu Bakr said, 'O Messenger of Allah, you have become gray.' He replied, 'Hud, Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, Amma Yatasa'alun and Idha Ash-Shamsu Kuwwirat have made me gray.'
h618.topic: Why the Prophet's hair turned gray

h619.text: When the verses about a multitude from the first ones and a few from the later ones were revealed, it was hard on the Companions. Then the verses about a multitude from the first ones and a multitude from the later ones were revealed, and the Prophet said, 'I hope that you will comprise a quarter of the residents of Paradise, a third of the residents of Paradise. Rather, you are half of the residents of Paradise, and will have a share in the other half.'
h619.topic: Believers of this Ummah among the people of Paradise

h620.text: The Prophet said, 'In Paradise there is a tree that a rider can travel under its shade for a hundred years but would not be able to pass it. Recite if you wish: "And in shade extended."'
h620.topic: The extended shade of a tree in Paradise

h621.text: The Prophet said, 'The first group to enter Paradise will be shining like the moon when it is full. The next group will be like the most radiant planet in the sky. They will not urinate, relieve nature, spit or blow their noses. Their combs will be of gold and their sweat of musk; and censers of aloeswood will be used. Their wives will be from the Hur al-Ayn. Their shape will be similar to one another, the shape of their father Adam, sixty cubits high in the sky.'
h621.topic: Description of the first to enter Paradise

h622.text: The sun was eclipsed and the Messenger of Allah led the people in the Eclipse prayer. They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we saw you reach out for something while standing, but then you stepped back.' He said, 'I saw Paradise and reached out for a cluster of fruit from it. Had I taken it, you would have kept eating from it for the remainder of the life of this world.'
h622.topic: The Prophet reaching for a cluster of fruit from Paradise

h623.text: The Prophet said, 'The fire that the Children of Adam kindle is one part out of seventy parts of the fire of Hell.' They said, 'O Messenger of Allah, this fire alone is sufficiently hot.' He said, 'The fire of Hell was made sixty-nine times hotter.'
h623.topic: Worldly fire compared to the fire of Hell

h624.text: The Prophet led the dawn prayer at Al-Hudaybiyah after a rainy night. When he finished he faced the people and said, 'Do you know what your Lord has said?' They replied, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'Allah has said: This morning some of My servants remained believers in Me and some became disbelievers. Whoever said the rain was due to the bounty and mercy of Allah believed in Me and disbelieved in the stars; and whoever said it rained because of a particular star disbelieved in Me and believed in that star.'
h624.topic: Attributing rain to Allah versus to the stars

h625.text: The Messenger of Allah said, 'He who likes to meet Allah, Allah likes to meet him; and he who hates to meet Allah, Allah hates to meet him.' The people wept and said they all hate death. He said it does not mean that; rather, when a believer near to Allah is dying, he is given the glad tidings of Rawh, Rayhan and a Garden of Delights, so he loves to meet Allah and Allah loves to meet him; but when a denier who went astray is dying, he is told of an entertainment of boiling water and entry into Hellfire, so he hates to meet Allah and Allah hates to meet him.
h625.topic: Loving to meet Allah at the time of death

h626.text: The Messenger of Allah said, 'Two statements that are light on the tongue, heavy on the Balance, and most beloved to the Most Merciful: Glory be to Allah and with His praise; glory be to Allah the Magnificent.'

h627.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to recite Al-Musabbihat before going to sleep, and he said: In them there is an Ayah that is better than a thousand Ayat.

h628.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would say this supplication when going to bed: O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Magnificent Throne, our Lord and the Lord of everything, Revealer of the Tawrah, the Injil and the Furqan, the Splitter of the grain of corn and the date stone, I seek refuge with You from the evil of everything whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are Al-Awwal, nothing is before You; Al-Akhir, nothing is after You; Az-Zahir, nothing is above You; and Al-Batin, nothing is below You. Remove the burden of debt from us and free us from poverty.

h629.text: The son of Adam claims, My wealth, my wealth. But is there anything belonging to you except that which you consumed, or which you wore and then it became worn, or which you gave as charity and so sent it forward? Other than that, you will go away and leave it behind for other people.

h630.text: The people of Paradise will look at the dwellers of the lofty mansions above them as one looks at a brilliant star far away on the horizon in the east or the west, because of their superiority over one another. The Companions asked whether these were the dwellings of the Prophets which none else could reach. He said: No, by Him in Whose Hand is my soul, they are for men who believed in Allah and believed in the Messengers.
h630.topic: Ranks of the believers in Paradise

h631.text: There are four ranks of martyrs. The first is a man who believes and is true in faith, who meets the enemy in battle, fulfills his duty to Allah and is killed; this is the one the people will look up to. The second is a believer who meets the enemy and is struck by a stray arrow which causes his death; he is in the second grade. The third is a believer who has combined good deeds with evil deeds, who meets the enemy and is true to his duty to Allah until he is killed. The fourth is a believer who has committed sins excessively, who meets the enemy and is true to his duty to Allah and is killed.

h632.text: Paradise is nearer to any of you than the strap of his sandal, and so is the Fire.
h632.topic: Nearness of Paradise and the Fire

h633.text: Allah ordained the measures of everything fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and His Throne was over the water.

h634.text: I was sent with the sword just before the Hour so that Allah be worshipped alone without partners. My provision was placed under the shadow of my spear, and those who defy my order were disgraced and humiliated, and whoever imitates a people is one of them.
h634.topic: Jihad and the establishment of Tawhid

h635.text: Every Prophet has a form of monasticism; the monasticism of this Ummah is Jihad in the cause of Allah, the Exalted and Most Honored.
h635.topic: Jihad as the monasticism of this Ummah

h636.text: Three will get their reward twice: a believer from the People of the Scripture who believed in his Prophet and then believed in me will get a double reward; a slave who fulfills the rights of Allah and the duties of his master will get a double reward; and a man who has a slave-girl, educates her well and teaches her good manners, then frees her and marries her, will get a double reward.
h636.topic: Those who receive a double reward

h637.text: Aishah said: All praise be to Allah, Whose hearing encompasses all voices. The woman who disputed came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and argued with him while I was in another part of the room and could not hear what she said. Then Allah revealed: 'Indeed Allah has heard the statement of her that disputes with you concerning her husband.'

h638.text: A man said: O Messenger of Allah, I pronounced Zihar against my wife, then had relations with her before paying the expiation. He (peace be upon him) said: May Allah grant you mercy, what made you do that? The man said: I saw her ornaments shining in the moonlight. The Prophet said: Then do not touch her until you do what Allah the Exalted has ordered you to do.
h638.topic: Not approaching wife before Zihar expiation

h639.text: Aishah said: Some Jews came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and greeted him saying, 'As-Sam alayka (death be upon you), O Abul-Qasim,' so I said to them, 'And upon you the death.' The Prophet said: O Aishah, Allah does not like rudeness and foul speech. I said: Did you not hear what they said? He said: Did you not hear that I answered them, 'And the same upon you?' Allah accepts our supplication against them, but not theirs against us.
h639.topic: Replying to the Jews' twisted greeting

h641.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: If you are three, then two of you should not hold a secret counsel apart from the third, because that would grieve him.
h641.topic: Forbidding two from whispering apart from a third

h642.text: Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) said: If you are three, then two of you should not hold a secret counsel apart from the third except with his permission, because that would grieve him.
h642.topic: Whispering apart from a third only with permission

h643.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: A man should not remove another man from his place and then sit in it. Rather spread out and make room, and Allah will make room for you.

h644.text: Umar bin Al-Khattab said that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah elevates some people by this Book and degrades others by it.
h644.topic: Allah raises and lowers people by the Quran

h645.text: Abu Ad-Darda said that he heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: There are no three in a village or desert among whom the prayer is not established but that Shaytan has gained mastery over them. So adhere to the congregation, for the wolf eats only the stray sheep.
h645.topic: Sticking to the congregation against Shaytan

h646.text: The Messenger of Allah ordered that the date trees of Bani An-Nadir be cut down and burned, and he had the date palms of Al-Buwayrah cut down.
h646.topic: Cutting the date trees of Bani An-Nadir

h647.text: Our property will not be inherited; whatever we leave behind is charity.
h647.topic: The Prophet's property is left as charity

h648.text: When I command you to do something, then do as much of it as you are able; and when I forbid you something, then abstain from it.
h648.topic: Obeying the commands and prohibitions of the Messenger

h649.text: A poor man came complaining of hunger, and the Prophet asked who would host him that night. An Ansari took him home, and he and his wife fed the guest while putting their children to sleep hungry and keeping the lamp off. In the morning the Prophet said that Allah wondered at, or laughed at, the action of that man and his wife, and this verse was revealed.
h649.topic: Selflessness of the Ansar in giving preference to others

h650.text: Beware of oppression, for oppression will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them.

h651.text: Whoever introduces a good practice in Islam has its reward and the reward of all who act upon it after him, without any decrease in their rewards; and whoever introduces an evil practice in Islam bears its burden and the burden of all who act upon it after him, without any decrease in their burdens.
h651.topic: Setting a good or evil example

h652.text: Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one; whoever preserves them will enter Paradise. He is One (Witr) and loves what is odd.

h653.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said regarding Hatib, 'He attended Badr. What can I tell you, perhaps Allah looked at those who attended Badr and said: O people of Badr, do what you like, for I have forgiven you.'
h653.topic: Forgiveness for the people of Badr

h654.text: A man asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, where is my father?' He said, 'In the Fire.' When the man turned away, the Prophet (peace be upon him) called him back and said, 'Verily, my father and your father are in the Fire.'
h654.topic: Kinship does not benefit the disbeliever

h655.text: Asma' asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother has come visiting and she desires something from me; should I keep good relations with her?' The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, keep good relations with your mother.'

h656.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to take the pledge from believing women by his word alone. 'A'ishah said that, by Allah, his hand never touched the hand of any woman while taking the pledge; he would only say, 'I have accepted your pledge.'
h656.topic: Manner of the women's pledge of allegiance

h657.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Pledge to me that you will not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit Zina, nor kill your children.' Then he said, 'Whoever among you fulfills this, his reward is with Allah. Whoever commits any of it and is punished for it, the punishment is an expiation for him. And whoever commits any of it and Allah screens him, then it is up to Allah: if He wills He forgives him, and if He wills He punishes him.'

h658.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took our pledge and recited to us the verse, 'that they will not associate anything with Allah,' and forbade us to wail over the dead.
h658.topic: Prohibition of wailing in the women's pledge

h659.text: I have several names: I am Muhammad, and I am Ahmad; I am Al-Mahi through whom Allah eliminates disbelief; I am Al-Hashir, the first to be resurrected, with the people gathered after me; and I am Al-Aqib (after whom there is no Prophet).
h659.topic: The names of the Prophet, including Ahmad

h660.text: There are three signs of a hypocrite: when he promises, he breaks his promise; when he speaks, he lies; and when he is entrusted, he betrays the trust.
h660.topic: Signs of a hypocrite include breaking a promise

h662.text: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) heard a mother tell her child she wished to give him something, he asked what she intended to give, and when she said dates, he said: If you had not given them to him, it would have been written against you as a lie.
h662.topic: Even a small unkept promise is recorded as a lie

h663.text: When asked about the first good news of his coming, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: The supplication of my father Ibrahim and the glad tidings given by Isa; and my mother saw a light come forth from her that lit up the palaces of Ash-Sham.
h663.topic: Isa's glad tidings of the Prophet's coming

h664.text: I was written with Allah as the Last and Final of the Prophets while Adam was still clay; and I will tell you of the first of that: the supplication of my father Ibrahim, the glad tidings of Isa about me, and the dream my mother saw, as the mothers of the Prophets see similar dreams.
h664.topic: The Prophet as the final Prophet foretold by Isa

h665.text: Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) used to recite Surat Al-Jumu'ah and Surat Al-Munafiqin during the Friday Prayer.

h666.text: While we were sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him), Surat Al-Jumu'ah was revealed to him, including 'And others among them who have not yet joined them.' They asked, 'Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?' He did not reply until they had asked three times. Salman Al-Farisi was among us, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) placed his hand on Salman and said, 'If faith were at the Pleiades, even then some men or a man from these people would attain it.'

h667.text: Abu Jahl said, 'If I see Muhammad praying at the Ka'bah, I will step on his neck.' When the Prophet (peace be upon him) heard of this he said, 'Had he done so, the angels would have snatched him away in public. Had the Jews wished for death, they would all have perished and seen their seats in the Fire. And had those who sought to invoke the curse of Allah with Allah's Messenger gone out, they would have returned to find no family or property.'
h667.topic: The Jews challenged to wish for death

h668.text: We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection, although the former nations were given the Scriptures before us. This was their day which Allah made compulsory for them, but they differed about it, so Allah guided us to it; and all other people come after us: the Jews tomorrow and the Christians the day after tomorrow.
h668.topic: Allah guided this Ummah to Friday

h669.text: Whoever takes a bath on Friday like the bath for sexual impurity and then goes in the first hour, it is as if he had sacrificed a camel; whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he had sacrificed a cow; whoever goes in the third hour, it is as if he had sacrificed a horned ram; whoever goes in the fourth hour, it is as if he had sacrificed a hen; and whoever goes in the fifth hour, it is as if he had offered an egg. When the Imam comes out, the angels attend to listen to the remembrance.
h669.topic: Reward for coming early to Jumu'ah

h670.text: Once a caravan arrived at Al-Madinah while Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) was giving the sermon, so the people left until only twelve men remained with him. Then Allah sent down the verse, 'And when they see some merchandise or some amusement, they disperse headlong to it.'
h670.topic: Leaving the sermon for a caravan

h671.text: Hypocrites have certain signs by which they are known: their greeting is really a curse, their food is from stealing and the war booty they collect is from theft. They shun the Masjid and do not come to the prayer but at its end. They are arrogant; it is neither easy for them to blend in, nor for people to blend with them. They are like pieces of wood by night and are noisy by day.

h672.text: When a man from the Emigrants and an Ansari man called out to their groups during a battle, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "What is this call of Jahiliyyah? Abandon it, for it is offensive." When Umar asked permission to strike off the head of Abdullah bin Ubay for his words, the Prophet said: "Leave him, lest the people say that Muhammad kills his companions."
h672.topic: Rejecting tribalism; the Prophet spares Ibn Ubay

h673.text: Amazing is the believer: there is no decree that Allah writes for him but it is better for him. If an affliction strikes him, he is patient and this is better for him; and if a bounty is granted to him, he is thankful and this is better for him. This trait is only for the faithful believer.
h673.topic: Every decree is good for the believer

h674.text: While the Messenger of Allah was giving a speech, Al-Hasan and Husayn came in wearing red shirts, walking and stumbling. He descended from the pulpit, took them, placed them before him and said: Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth: 'Verily, your wealth and your children are a Fitnah.' I saw these two boys walking and stumbling and could not be patient until I stopped my speech and picked them up.

h675.text: When I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can; and whatever I forbid you, then avoid it.
h675.topic: Obey commands as much as you are able

h677.text: Order him to take her back and keep her until she is clean from her menses, and then to wait until she gets her next period and becomes clean again. Then, if he wishes to divorce her, he can divorce her when she is clean from her menses, before he has sexual intercourse with her. This is the 'Iddah which Allah has fixed for the women being divorced.
h677.topic: Divorcing a wife at the prescribed period

h678.text: There is no obligation on him to spend on you, nor housing. And he ordered her to complete her waiting period in another house, saying: She is a woman my Companions visit; spend this period in the house of Ibn Umm Maktum, for he is a blind man and cannot see you when you take off your garments.
h678.topic: No maintenance or housing for the irrevocably divorced woman

h679.text: O boy, I will teach you some words. Be mindful of Allah and He will protect you; be mindful of Allah and you will find Him before you. If you ask, ask Allah, and if you seek help, seek it from Allah. Know that if the whole nation gathered to benefit you, they would not benefit you except with what Allah has decreed for you, and if they gathered to harm you, they would not harm you except with what Allah has decreed against you. The pens have been lifted and the pages have dried.
h679.topic: Reliance upon Allah and trust in His decree

h680.text: The husband of Subay'ah Al-Aslamiyyah died while she was pregnant, and she gave birth a short time after his death. When she had completed her postnatal term she sought the verdict of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) about remarrying, and he permitted her to marry once she had delivered her child.
h680.topic: The waiting period of a pregnant woman ends at childbirth

h681.text: Had she taken out what was in her mortar and not emptied it fully by shaking it, it would have continued crushing the seeds until the Day of Resurrection.

h682.text: Whoever usurps the land of somebody unjustly, even if it was a mere hand span, then his neck will be encircled with it down to the seven earths.
h682.topic: The seven earths and the gravity of seizing land unjustly

h683.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh. When 'A'ishah and Hafsah, having agreed together, told him they smelled Maghafir on him, he said, 'No, but I drank honey, and I will never drink it again,' and asked that this not be disclosed to anyone.
h683.topic: Reason for the prohibition of honey

h684.text: When 'Umar urged the Prophet (peace be upon him) to ask Allah to make his followers prosperous, noting that the Persians and Byzantines were given worldly luxuries though they did not worship Allah, the Prophet sat up and said, 'O Ibn al-Khattab, do you have any doubt? These are a people who have been given the good things of their life in this world only.' The Prophet had also sworn not to go to his wives for one month because of his anger toward them.
h684.topic: The Prophet's seclusion from his wives

h685.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Order the children to pray when they reach the age of seven, and when they reach the age of ten, discipline them for not performing it.'

h686.text: A man who prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) during the year of the Conquest of Makkah heard him say, 'O Allah, do not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection.'
h686.topic: Seeking refuge from disgrace on the Day of Resurrection

h687.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) drew four lines on the ground and asked, 'Do you know what these represent?' They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'The best among the women of Paradise are Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Maryam bint 'Imran, and Asiyah bint Muzahim, the wife of Fir'awn.'

h688.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Many men have reached the level of perfection, but none among women reached it except Asiyah the wife of Fir'awn, Maryam the daughter of 'Imran, and Khadijah the daughter of Khuwaylid; and the superiority of 'A'ishah over other women is like the superiority of Tharid over other foods.'

h689.text: The first of what Allah created was the Pen, and He said to it: Write. The Pen said: O my Lord, what shall I write? He said: Write the decree and whatever will be throughout eternity.

h690.text: Sa'd bin Hisham asked Aishah about the character of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and she replied: Have you not read the Qur'an? Verily, the character of the Messenger of Allah was the Qur'an.
h690.topic: The Prophet's character was the Qur'an

h691.text: I served the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, for ten years, and he never said a word of displeasure to me, nor did he ever say concerning something I had done, Why did you do that, nor concerning something I had not done, Why did you not do this. He had the best character.

h692.text: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, had the most handsome face of all the people, and he had the best behavior of all the people. And he was not tall, nor was he short.
h692.topic: The Prophet's noble appearance and conduct

h693.text: I have only been sent to perfect righteous behavior.
h693.topic: The Prophet sent to perfect good character

h694.text: The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, passed by two graves and said: Verily, these two are being punished, and they are not being punished for something major. One of them was not careful about protecting himself from urine, and the other one used to spread Namimah (tale-bearing).
h694.topic: Punishment of the grave for tale-bearing

h695.text: Shall I inform you of the people of Paradise? Every weak and oppressed person; when he swears by Allah, he fulfills his oath. Shall I inform you of the people of the Fire? Every Utul (cruel person), Jawwaz and arrogant person.
h695.topic: The cruel and arrogant among the people of the Fire

h696.text: Our Lord will reveal His Shin, and every believing male and female will prostrate to Him. The only ones who will remain are those who prostrated in the worldly life only to be seen and heard; this person will try to prostrate, but his back will become one stiff plate that will not bend.
h696.topic: Prostration on the Day of Judgement

h697.text: The evil eye is real. If anything were to overtake the divine decree, it would be the evil eye. And if you are asked to wash (to remove its effect), then wash well.
h697.topic: The reality of the evil eye

h698.text: Verily, the evil eye is real.
h698.topic: The reality of the evil eye

h699.text: I was helped by an easterly wind and the people of 'Ad were destroyed by a westerly wind.
h699.topic: How the people of 'Ad were destroyed

h700.text: Allah will bring the servant close to Him on the Day of Judgement and make him confess all of his sins, until the servant thinks that he is about to be destroyed. Then Allah will say: I concealed these sins for you in the worldly life and I forgive you for them today. Then he will be given his book of good deeds in his right hand.
h700.topic: Allah forgiving the believer in private on Judgement Day

h701.text: Verily, Paradise has one hundred levels, and between each level is a distance like the distance between the earth and the sky.

h702.text: Work deeds, strive, and seek to draw near to Allah, and know that none of you will be admitted into Paradise because of his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of Allah? He replied: Not even me, unless Allah covers me with mercy from Himself and grace.

h703.text: The people will be exhibited three times on the Day of Judgement. The first two presentations will be arguing and offering excuses. During the third presentation the records will fly into their hands; some will receive their records in their right hands and some will receive them in their left hands.
h703.topic: Being presented before Allah on Judgement Day

h704.text: If a drop of lead like this were sent from the heaven to the earth, a distance of five hundred years of travel, it would reach the earth before night. And if it were sent from the head of the chain of Hell, it would travel forty fall seasons, night and day, before it would reach its base.
h704.topic: The chain of Hell described in the surah

h705.text: There is not any owner of treasure who does not pay its due except that it will be made into heated metal plates and branded upon him in the fire of Hell. His forehead, side and back will be scorched with these plates. This will continue until Allah judges between His servants on a Day whose measure is fifty thousand years of what you count. Then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to the Fire.
h705.topic: Punishment for withholding Zakah and the Day of fifty thousand years

h707.text: The worst thing that can be in a man is greedy impatience and unrestrained cowardice.
h707.topic: Blameworthy traits of greed and cowardice

h710.text: Why do I see you in separate groups?
h710.topic: Disapproval of sitting scattered in groups

h716.text: Anas was asked about the recitation of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), and he replied that the Prophet used to elongate the letters; he then recited the Basmalah, elongating 'In the Name of Allah,' 'the Most Gracious,' and 'the Most Merciful.'

h717.text: A'ishah related that Al-Harith bin Hisham asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) how revelation came to him. He replied that sometimes it came like the ringing of a bell, which was the most severe upon him, and then it would pass after he had grasped what was inspired; and sometimes the angel came to him in the form of a man and spoke to him so that he grasped what he said. A'ishah added that she saw sweat dropping from his forehead on a very cold day as the revelation ended.
h717.topic: How revelation came to the Prophet

h718.text: A'ishah described the night prayer of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him): his Siwak and ablution water would be prepared, and when Allah awakened him he would clean his teeth, perform ablution, and pray eight units without sitting except at the eighth, where he would sit, remember Allah and supplicate, then stand without the Taslim and pray a ninth unit before sitting, supplicating, and giving the greeting of peace aloud; he would then pray two units while sitting, making eleven in all. When he grew older and heavier he prayed Witr with seven units and two more while sitting, making nine.
h718.topic: The Prophet's night prayer and Witr

h719.text: Abdullah reported that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) asked, 'Which of you holds his wealth to be more beloved to him than the wealth of his heir?' They said that every one of them held his own wealth dearer. He told them to consider what they were saying, then said, 'The wealth of one of you is only that which he sends forth, and the wealth of his heir is that which he leaves behind.'
h719.topic: One's true wealth is what is sent forth

h720.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to a man that five prayers during a day and a night are obligatory. The man asked whether anything other than these was obligatory upon him, and the Prophet replied, 'No, except what you may do voluntarily.'
h720.topic: Five daily prayers are obligatory, the rest voluntary

h721.text: Abdullah bin Amr asked the Prophet (peace be upon him) whether he felt anything when revelation came to him. The Messenger of Allah replied, 'I hear a ringing, and then I remain quiet when that occurs. There has not been a single time that revelation has come to me except that I thought my soul was about to be taken.'
h721.topic: The Prophet's experience of receiving revelation

h722.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: While I was walking I heard a voice from the sky. I lifted my gaze and saw the same angel who had come to me at the cave of Hira, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I fled from him in fear until I fell to the ground. Then I came to my family and said, 'Wrap me up, wrap me up,' so they wrapped me up. Then Allah revealed, 'O you wrapped up! Arise and warn! And magnify your Lord. And purify your garments. And keep away from Ar-Rujz.' After this the revelation started coming strongly and frequently in succession.

h723.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: How can I be comfortable when the one with the horn has placed it in his mouth, leaned his forehead forward, and is waiting to be commanded so that he can blow? The Companions said, 'What do you command us, O Messenger of Allah?' He replied: Say, 'Allah is sufficient for us, and what an excellent Trustee He is. We put our trust in Allah.'

h724.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him), describing the Frequented House (Al-Bayt Al-Ma'mur) in the seventh heaven, said: Seventy thousand angels enter into it every day and they do not return to it again.

h725.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to struggle hard to grasp the revelation and would move his lips rapidly along with it. Then Allah revealed, "Move not your tongue concerning it to make haste therewith. It is for Us to collect it and that it be recited." So afterwards, when Jibril would come to him he would stay silent and listen, and when Jibril had left he would recite it just as he had been taught.
h725.topic: How the Prophet received the revelation

h726.narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) and Abu Hurairah (RA)
h726.text: Some people asked, "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Judgement?" He said, "Are you harmed by seeing the sun and the moon when there are no clouds beneath them?" They replied, "No." He said, "Then you will surely see your Lord like that."
h726.topic: Believers will see their Lord in the Hereafter

isnad.name: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (RA) and Abu Hurairah (RA)

h727.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) looked at the full moon and said, "Verily, you will see your Lord just as you see this moon. So if you are able to avoid missing a prayer before the rising of the sun and a prayer before its setting, then do so."
h727.topic: Seeing the Lord like the full moon

h728.text: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allah will say, "Do you want me to give you anything extra?" They will say, "Have You not whitened our faces? Have You not entered us into Paradise and saved us from the Fire?" Then He will remove the veil, and they will not be given anything more beloved to them than looking at their Lord; and that is the extra (Ziyadah).
h728.topic: The reward of looking at the Lord in Paradise

h729.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to Abu Jahl, "Woe to you, and then woe to you! Again woe to you, and then woe to you!" Then Allah revealed this verse.

h730.text: Whenever the verse "Is it not so then, that He would be able to give life to the dead?" was recited, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) would say, "Glory be to You, of course (yes)."

h731.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite in the Morning (Fajr) prayer on Friday Surat As-Sajdah (Alif Lam Mim, the revelation...) and Surat Al-Insan (Has there not been over man...).
h731.topic: Reciting As-Sajdah and Al-Insan in Friday Fajr

h732.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: All of mankind wakes up in the morning the merchant of his own soul; so he either imprisons it or sets it free.
h732.topic: Every person sells his own soul

h733.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever makes a vow to obey Allah, then let him obey Him; and whoever makes a vow to disobey Allah, then let him not disobey Him.
h733.topic: Fulfilling a vow of obedience to Allah

h737.text: Ibn Mas'ud said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah in a cave at Mina, Surat Al-Mursalat was revealed to him, and he was reciting it while I learned it from his mouth. A snake leaped out at us, and the Prophet said, "Kill it!" We rushed after it but it escaped. Then the Prophet said, "It was saved from your harm just as you were saved from its harm."
h737.topic: Revelation of Al-Mursalat in the cave at Mina

h738.text: Umm al-Fadl heard the Prophet reciting Surat Al-Mursalat in the Maghrib prayer, and she said that it was the last thing she heard the Messenger of Allah recite, for he recited it in the Maghrib prayer before he died.
h738.topic: Prophet reciting Al-Mursalat in Maghrib prayer

h740.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to recite Surat Al-A'la and Surat Al-Ghashiyah in the Eid and Friday prayers. An-Nu'man bin Bashir reported that the Prophet would recite Al-Ghashiyah on Friday along with Surat Al-Jumu'ah.
h740.topic: Reciting Al-Ghashiyah in Friday and Eid prayers

h741.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: The rivers of Paradise spring forth from beneath hills, or mountains, of musk.
h741.topic: The rivers of Paradise flow from musk

h742.text: A bedouin came questioning the Prophet (peace be upon him), asking who created the heaven, the earth, and erected the mountains, and the Prophet answered that Allah did. The man then affirmed each obligation the Prophet conveyed to him, and as he left he swore he would neither add to nor decrease from them. The Prophet said: If he has spoken truthfully, he will certainly enter Paradise.
h742.topic: The bedouin who affirmed the pillars of Islam

h743.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say La ilaha illallah. So if they say it, they have safeguarded their blood and wealth from me, except for what is rightfully due from it, and their reckoning is with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then he recited: So remind them, you are only one who reminds. You are not a Musaytir over them.
h743.topic: The Prophet only reminds; reckoning belongs to Allah

h744.text: A man joined Muadh in prayer, but Muadh prolonged it, so the man left and prayed alone, then went to tend his she-camel. When Muadh called him a hypocrite and informed the Prophet (peace be upon him), the Prophet said to Muadh, 'Are you causing trouble, Muadh? Why don't you recite Glorify the Name of your Lord the Most High, By the sun and its brightness, By the dawn, and By the night as it envelops?'

h745.text: There are no days in which righteous deeds are more beloved to Allah than these days, meaning the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. They asked, 'Not even fighting Jihad in the way of Allah?' He replied, 'Not even Jihad in the way of Allah, except for a man who goes out with his self and his wealth and does not return with any of that.'
h745.topic: Virtue of the ten days of Dhul-Hijjah

h746.text: The guardian of the orphan and I will be like these two in Paradise. And he put his two fingers together, the middle finger and the index finger.

h747.text: Hell will be brought near on that Day, and it will have seventy thousand leashes, and each leash will have seventy thousand angels pulling it.
h747.topic: Hell brought forth on the Day of Judgement

h748.text: This verse was revealed while Abu Bakr was sitting with the Prophet (peace be upon him). Abu Bakr said, 'O Messenger of Allah, there is nothing better than this.' The Prophet replied, 'This will indeed be said to you.'
h748.topic: Glad tidings for the tranquil soul

h749.text: Verily, Allah made this city (Makkah) sacred on the Day that He created the heavens and the earth. Therefore, it is sacred by the sanctity of Allah until the Day of Judgement. Its trees should not be uprooted, and its bushes and grasses should not be removed. And it was only made lawful for me to fight in for one hour of a day. Today its sanctity has been restored just as it was sacred yesterday. So, let the one who is present inform those who are absent.
h749.source: Agreed upon (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

isnad.name: Agreed upon (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

h750.text: Whoever frees a believing slave, Allah will free for every limb of the slave one of his limbs from the Fire, to such an extent that He will free a hand for a hand, a leg for a leg, and a private part for a private part.
h750.topic: Reward for freeing a believing slave

h751.text: Whoever builds a Masjid so that Allah may be remembered in it, Allah will build a house for him in Paradise; and whoever frees a Muslim person, then it will be his ransom from Hell; and whoever grows grey in Islam, then it will be a light for him on the Day of Judgement.
h751.topic: Freeing a Muslim as a ransom from Hell

h752.text: Whoever has three children born to him in Islam, and they die before reaching the age of puberty, Allah will enter him into Paradise by virtue of His mercy to them. And whoever grows gray in the way of Allah, then it will be a light for him on the Day of Judgement. And whoever shoots an arrow in the way of Allah that reaches the enemy, whether it hits or misses, he will get the reward of freeing a slave. And whoever frees a believing slave, then Allah will free each of his limbs from the Fire for every limb that the slave has. And whoever equipped two riding animals in the way of Allah, then indeed Paradise has eight gates, and Allah will allow him to enter any of them he chooses.
h752.topic: The reward of freeing a believing slave

h753.text: Charity given to the poor person is counted as one charity, while if it is given to a relative it is counted as two: charity and connecting the ties of kinship.
h753.topic: Charity to a relative carries a double reward

h754.text: Whoever does not show mercy to our children, nor does he recognize the right of our elders, then he is not of us.
h754.topic: Showing mercy and recognizing the rights of others

h755.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to Mu'adh: "Why did you not pray with (the recitation of) 'Glorify the Name of your Lord the Most High' (87), 'By the sun and its brightness' (91), and 'By the night as it envelops' (92)?"

h756.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Every child that is born, is born upon the Fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian. This is just as the animal is born complete with all of its parts. Do you notice any mutilation in it?"
h756.topic: Every child is born upon the Fitrah

h757.text: Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: "Verily I created My servants as monotheists, but then the devils came to them and distracted them from their religion."

h758.text: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) whether people's actions are preordained for them or written only after the Message comes to them. He replied: "Rather it is something preordained for them." The man said: "Then what is the point of our actions?" He replied: "Whoever Allah created for one of the two positions (Paradise or Hell), He makes it easy for him to attain. The proof of that is in the Book of Allah: 'By the soul and Him Who apportioned it, then He showed it its transgression and its piety.'"

h759.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "O Allah! Verily I seek refuge with You from weakness, laziness, senility, cowardliness, stinginess and the torment of the grave. O Allah! Give my soul its good and purify it, for You are the best to purify it; You are its Guardian and Master. O Allah! Verily I seek refuge with You from a heart that is not humble, a soul that is not satisfied, knowledge that does not benefit, and a supplication that is not answered."

h760.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) gave a sermon in which he mentioned the she-camel and the man who killed her. He said, regarding "When their most wicked went forth": "A strong and mighty man who was invincible among his tribe, like Abu Zam'ah, went forth to her."

h761.text: While the Companions were with the Messenger of Allah at the cemetery of Baqi' Al-Gharqad for a funeral, he said: There is none among you except that his place has already been written, a seat in Paradise and a seat in the Hellfire. They asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, should we depend on this?' He replied: Perform deeds, for everyone will have the deeds of what he was created for made easy for him. Then he recited: 'As for him who gives and has Taqwa, and believes in Al-Husna, We will make smooth for him the path of ease,' up to '...the path to evil.'
h761.topic: Deeds made easy according to one's predestined end

h762.text: Jabir bin 'Abdullah asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, are we performing deeds for something that has already been predetermined, or is the matter based upon what we are just doing now?' The Prophet replied: It is a matter that has been predetermined. Suraqah asked, 'Then what is the purpose of deeds?' The Messenger of Allah said: Everyone who does deeds will have his deeds made easy for him.
h762.topic: Predestination and the purpose of deeds

h763.text: 'Umar asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, do you think that the deeds we do are a matter already predetermined, or something just beginning or new?' The Prophet replied: It is something that has already been predetermined. Therefore work deeds, O son of Al-Khattab, for each person will have things made easy for him. So whoever is of the people of happiness will work deeds for happiness, and whoever is of the people of misery will work deeds for misery.

h764.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Verily, the person punished lightest of the people of the Fire on the Day of Judgement will be a man who will have placed on the soles of his feet two coals that will cause his brain to boil.
h764.topic: The lightest punishment in the Fire

h765.text: The Messenger of Allah said: All of my followers will enter Paradise on the Day of Judgement except for whoever refuses. They asked, 'Who would refuse, O Messenger of Allah?' He replied: Whoever obeys me will enter Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused.
h765.topic: Obedience to the Prophet as the path to Paradise

h766.text: The Messenger of Allah said: Whoever equipped two riding animals in the way of Allah, the Gatekeepers of Paradise will call to him saying, 'O servant of Allah, this is good.' Abu Bakr said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the one called from them will have no need. Will there be anyone who will be called from all of them?' The Prophet replied: Yes, and I hope that you will be one of them.
h766.topic: Reward for spending in the way of Allah

h767.text: The Prophet became ill, so he did not stand for prayer for a night or two. Then a woman came and said, 'O Muhammad! I think that your devil has finally left you.' So Allah revealed: By the forenoon. By the night when it darkens. Your Lord has neither forsaken you nor hates you.
h767.topic: Reason for revelation of Surat Ad-Duha

h768.text: Wealth is not determined by abundance of possessions, but wealth is the richness of the soul.
h768.topic: True richness is contentment of the soul

h769.text: Whoever accepts Islam, is provided with his basic needs, and Allah makes him content with what He has given him, then he will be successful.
h769.topic: Success through contentment with one's provision

h770.text: I have nothing to do with this world. The parable of me and this world is like a rider who rests in the shade of a tree, then he passes on and leaves it.
h770.topic: The Prophet's detachment from worldly life

h771.text: Whoever is not thankful to the people, then he is not thankful to Allah.
h771.topic: Gratitude to people is part of gratitude to Allah

h772.text: Whoever overcomes some test (calamity) and mentions it to others, then he is indeed thankful; and whoever conceals it, then indeed he was ungrateful.
h772.topic: Mentioning Allah's favors as an expression of thanks

h775.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite Surat At-Tin ("By the fig and the olive") in one of his Rak'ahs while traveling. Al-Bara' bin 'Azib said he never heard anyone with a nicer voice or recitation than him.
h775.topic: Reciting Surat At-Tin in prayer while traveling

h776.text: Revelation began for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) with true dreams that came to pass like the breaking of dawn. Then he loved seclusion and would withdraw to the cave of Hira to worship. The angel came to him there and said, 'Read!' He replied, 'I am not one who reads.' The angel seized and pressed him, then released him and again said, 'Read!', repeating this until he recited 'Read in the Name of your Lord who has created,' up to 'that which he knew not.' He returned with his heart trembling to Khadijah saying, 'Wrap me up, wrap me up,' until his fear left him.
h776.topic: The first revelation in the cave of Hira

h777.text: Abu Jahl said, 'If I see Muhammad praying at the Ka'bah, I will stomp on his neck.' This reached the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said, 'If he does, he will be seized by the angels.'
h777.topic: Abu Jahl's threat against the Prophet's prayer

h778.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was praying at the Station of Ibrahim when Abu Jahl passed by and rebuked him, threatening him. The Prophet (peace be upon him) reprimanded him. Abu Jahl said, 'What can you threaten me with? By Allah, I have the most kinsmen of this valley with me.' Then Allah revealed, 'Then let him call upon his council. We will call out the guards of Hell.'
h778.topic: Abu Jahl boasting of his supporters

h779.text: When Abu Jahl resolved to stomp on the Prophet's neck while he prayed and approached to do so, he suddenly turned back on his heels shielding himself with his hands. Asked what was wrong, he said that between himself and the Prophet was a ditch of fire and terrors and wings. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, 'If he had come near me, the angels would have snatched him limb by limb.'
h779.topic: The angels protecting the Prophet from Abu Jahl

h780.text: The closest that a servant can be to his Lord is when he is in prostration, so make abundant supplications while prostrating.

h781.text: Whoever stands in prayer during the Night of Al-Qadr with faith and expecting reward from Allah will be forgiven for his previous sins.
h781.topic: Reward for praying on the Night of Al-Qadr

h782.text: The Prophet performed I'tikaf during the first ten nights of Ramadan, then the middle ten, and then said: Whoever performed I'tikaf with me, let him come back, for I saw the Night of Al-Qadr but was caused to forget it, and indeed it is during the last ten nights, on an odd night; and I saw myself as if I were prostrating in mud and water. That morning it rained and the traces of mud and water were seen on his forehead, confirming his dream.
h782.topic: The Night of Al-Qadr is in the last ten nights

h783.text: Seek it in the last ten nights of Ramadan. In the ninth it still remains, in the seventh it still remains, in the fifth it still remains.
h783.topic: Seeking the Night of Al-Qadr in the last ten nights

h784.text: The Prophet indicated that the Night of Al-Qadr is the twenty-seventh night, its sign being that the sun rises the next morning without rays upon it.
h784.topic: The sign of the Night of Al-Qadr

h785.text: Aishah asked: O Messenger of Allah, if I find the Night of Al-Qadr, what should I say? He replied: Say: O Allah, verily You are the Pardoning, You love to pardon, so pardon me.
h785.topic: Supplication for the Night of Al-Qadr

h786.text: The month of Ramadan has come to you. It is a blessed month which Allah has obligated you to fast. During it the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell are closed and the devils are shackled. In it there is a night that is better than one thousand months. Whoever is deprived of its good has truly been deprived.
h786.topic: A night better than a thousand months in Ramadan

h787.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said to Ubayy bin Ka'b, "Verily, Allah has commanded me to recite to you: 'Those who disbelieve from among the People of the Scripture.'" Ubayy said, "He (Allah) mentioned me by name to you?" The Prophet (peace be upon him) replied, "Yes." So Ubayy cried.
h787.topic: Allah commanded the Prophet to recite this Surah to Ubayy

h788.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Shall I not inform you of the best of creation?" They said, "Of course, O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "A man who takes the reins of his horse in the way of Allah, and whenever there is a fearful cry from the enemy, he climbs upon it. Shall I not inform you of the best of creation?" They said, "Of course, O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "A man who has a flock of sheep and he establishes the prayer and gives the obligatory charity. Shall I not inform you of the worst of creation?" They said, "Of course." He said, "The person who is asked by Allah and he does not give by Him."
h788.topic: The best and worst of creation

h789.text: A man asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) to teach him something comprehensive to recite, so the Prophet taught him Surat Az-Zalzalah (When the earth quakes with its Zilzal). After reciting it, the man swore he would never add anything else to it and turned to leave, and the Prophet said, 'The little man has been successful, the little man has been successful.'

h790.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said that the earth will throw out the pieces of its liver, its contents, and gold and silver will come out like columns. A murderer will come and say, 'I killed for this?' The one who severed ties of kinship will say, 'For this I severed the ties of kinship?' The thief will say, 'For this I got my hands amputated?' Then they will leave it and take nothing from it.
h790.topic: The earth casts out its treasures

h791.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited the verse (That Day it will declare its information) and asked, 'Do you know what is its information?' They said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said, 'Its information is that it will testify against every male and female servant about what they did upon its surface, saying that he did such and such on such and such a day. So this is its information.'

h792.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was asked about donkeys and said, 'Allah has not revealed anything concerning them except this single, comprehensive verse: So whosoever does good equal to the weight of a speck of dust shall see it, and whosoever does evil equal to the weight of a speck of dust shall see it.'
h792.topic: Every atom's weight of deeds is recompensed

h793.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'Ward off the Fire, even if by giving half a date in charity, and even by saying a single good word.'
h793.topic: No good deed is too small

h794.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to say, 'O Aishah! Beware of the sins that are belittled, for indeed they will be taken account of by Allah.'

h795.text: The fire of the children of Adam that you kindle is one part of the seventy parts of the fire of Hell. The Companions said, "O Messenger of Allah, would it not have been sufficient?" He replied that it is greater than it by sixty-nine times, each part like its heat.

h796.text: Verily, the person who will receive the lightest torment of the people of the Hellfire will be a man who will have two sandals that will cause his brain to boil.
h796.topic: The lightest punishment in the Fire

h797.text: The Hellfire complained to its Lord saying, "O Lord, some parts of me devour other parts of me." So Allah permitted it to take two breaths, one breath in the winter and one breath in the summer. Thus, the most severe cold you experience in winter is from its cold, and the most severe heat you experience in summer is from its heat.
h797.topic: The two breaths of the Hellfire

h798.text: When the heat becomes intense, pray the prayer when it cools down, for indeed the intense heat is from the breath of Hell.

h799.text: If the Son of Adam had a valley of gold, he would desire another like it.

h800.text: The servant says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Yet he only gets three benefits from his wealth: that which he eats and finishes, that which he wears until it is worn out, or that which he gives in charity and it is spent. Everything else other than that will go away and leave him for the people.

h801.text: Three things follow the deceased person, and two of them return while one remains behind with him. The things which follow him are his family, his wealth and his deeds. His family and his wealth return while his deeds remain.

h802.text: The Son of Adam becomes old with senility, but yet two things remain with him: greed and hope.
h802.topic: Greed and hope persist with age

h803.text: Two favors are treated unjustly by most people: health and free time.
h803.topic: Health and free time are favors

h804.text: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says on the Day of Judgement: 'O Son of Adam! I made you ride upon the horses and camels, I gave you women to marry, and I made you reside and rule. So where is the thanks for that?'

h805.text: This is the prayer of the hypocrite, this is the prayer of the hypocrite, this is the prayer of the hypocrite. He sits watching the sun until it is between the two horns of Shaytan. Then he stands and pecks four (Rak'ahs), and he does not remember Allah in them except very little.

h806.text: Whoever tries to make the people hear of his deed, Allah, the One Who hears His creation, will hear it and make him despised and degraded.
h806.topic: Warning against showing off in deeds

h807.text: While we were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) in the Masjid, he dozed off, then lifted his head smiling. We asked what made him laugh. He said: 'A Surah was just revealed to me,' and recited: 'Verily, We have granted you Al-Kawthar. Therefore turn in prayer to your Lord and sacrifice. For he who hates you, he will be cut off.' Then he asked: 'Do you know what is Al-Kawthar?' We said, 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'It is a river that my Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, has promised me, and it has abundant goodness. It is a pond where my Ummah will be brought on the Day of Judgement. Its containers are as numerous as the stars in the sky.'
h807.topic: Revelation of the Surah and the meaning of Al-Kawthar

h808.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'I entered Paradise and came to a river whose banks had tents made of pearls. So I thrust my hand into its flowing water and found that it was the strongest musk. I asked, "O Jibril! What is this?" He replied, "This is Al-Kawthar which Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has given you."'
h808.topic: Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise

h809.text: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) was taken up to the heaven, he said: 'I came to a river whose banks had domes of hollowed pearl. I said, "O Jibril! What is this?" He replied, "This is Al-Kawthar."'

h810.text: A man asked, 'O Messenger of Allah! What is Al-Kawthar?' He replied: 'It is a river in Paradise which my Lord has given me. It is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey. There are birds in it whose necks are long like carrots.' Umar said, 'O Messenger of Allah! They will be beautiful.' The Prophet (peace be upon him) replied: 'The one who eats them will be more beautiful than them, O Umar.'

h811.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise whose banks are of gold and it runs over pearls. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey.'

h812.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited this Surah (Al-Kafirun) and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Surat Al-Ikhlas) in the two Rak'ahs of Tawaf.
h812.topic: Recitation in the two Rak'ahs of Tawaf

h813.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) recited these two Surahs (Al-Kafirun and Al-Ikhlas) in the two Rak'ahs of the optional Morning prayer.
h813.topic: Recitation in the two Rak'ahs before Fajr

h814.text: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite 'Say: O disbelievers' (Al-Kafirun) and 'Say: He is Allah, One' (Al-Ikhlas) in the two Rak'ahs before the Morning prayer and the two Rak'ahs after the Sunset prayer.
h814.topic: Recitation before Fajr and after Maghrib

h815.text: When this surah was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "My death has been announced to me." And indeed he died during that year.
h815.topic: The surah as a sign of the Prophet's approaching death

h816.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to say often in his bowing and prostrating: "Glory to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You. O Allah, forgive me." He did this as his implementation of the Qur'an.
h816.topic: The Prophet glorifying and seeking forgiveness in prayer

h817.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to often say towards the end of his life: "Glory to Allah, and praise be unto Him. I seek Allah's forgiveness and I repent to Him." And he said: "Verily, my Lord has informed me that I will see a sign in my Ummah, and He has commanded me that when I see it, I should glorify His praises and seek His forgiveness, for He is the One Who accepts repentance. And indeed I have seen it."
h817.topic: The Prophet seeking forgiveness upon seeing the promised sign

h818.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Verily, the people have entered into the religion of Allah in crowds, and they will also leave it in crowds."
h818.topic: People entering and leaving the religion in crowds

h819.text: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was suffering from an ailment, he would recite the Mu'awwidhatayn over himself and blow over himself; and when his pain became severe, 'A'ishah would recite them over him and wipe his own hand over him, seeking the blessing of those Surahs.
h819.topic: Reciting the Mu'awwidhatayn for protection and healing

h820.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: "Do you not see that there have been Ayat revealed to me tonight the like of which has not been seen before?" referring to "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq" and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind."
h820.topic: The unmatched virtue of the two Surahs of refuge

h821.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) was bewitched until he imagined that he had relations with his wives when he had not. He said that Allah had answered his prayer: two men came to him, one sitting at his head and one at his feet, and one asked the other what was wrong with him; the reply was that he was bewitched by Labid bin A'sam, using a comb and hair placed in the dried bark of a male date palm under a rock in the well of Dharwan. He went to the well and removed it, and said its water was as if henna had been soaked in it and its palm trees were like the heads of devils. When asked if he would make it public, he said: "Allah has cured me, and I hate to spread wickedness among any of the people."
h821.topic: The bewitchment of the Prophet and his cure

h822.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) used to seek protection against the evil eyes of the Jinn and mankind; but when the Mu'awwidhatayn were revealed, he used them for protection and abandoned all else besides them.
h822.topic: Adopting the two Surahs as the means of seeking refuge

h823.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) taught 'Uqbah to recite "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of Al-Falaq" and "Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind," describing them as among the best two Surahs that people recite, and said: "Recite these two Surahs whenever you go to sleep and whenever you get up."
h823.topic: The Prophet teaching the two Surahs and when to recite them

h824.text: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) took 'A'ishah by her hand and showed her the moon when it rose, and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the evil of this Ghasiq when it becomes dark."
h824.topic: Seeking refuge from the evil of the Ghasiq

h826.text: While the Prophet (peace be upon him) was walking Safiyyah bint Huyay back to her home at night during I'tikaf, two men of the Ansar passed by and hurried on when they saw him. He said, "Slow down! This is Safiyyah bint Huyay." They said, "Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "Verily, Shaytan runs in the Son of Adam like the running of the blood, and I feared that he might cast something evil into your hearts."
h826.topic: Shaytan flows through man like blood

h827.text: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and said, "O Messenger of Allah! Sometimes I say things to myself that I would rather fall from the sky than say aloud." The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "Allah is Most Great! Allah is Most Great! All praise is due to Allah Who sent his (Shaytan's) plot back as only a whisper."
h827.topic: Reducing Shaytan's plot to a mere whisper
